exceptions: appropriations or expenditures for ordinary repair and maintenance of the State Capitol building, fixtures and furniture

provisions.what: The supreme executive power of this State is vested in the Governor
The Governor shall see that the law is faithfully executed

The Governor shall be elected every fourth year at the same time and places as members of the Assembly and hold office from the Monday after January 1 following the election until a successor qualifies
The Governor shall be an elector who has been a citizen of the United States and a resident of this State for 5 years immediately preceding the Governor’s election
requires: an elector
a citizen of the United States and a resident of this State for 5 years immediately preceding the Governor’s election

provisions.what: The Governor may not hold other public office
forbids: hold other public office

provisions.what: No Governor may serve more than 2 terms
forbids: serve more than 2 terms

provisions.what: The Governor shall report to the Legislature each calendar year on the condition of the State
The Governor may make recommendations
The Governor may require executive officers and agencies and their employees to furnish information relating to their duties
The Governor may fill a vacancy in office by appointment until a successor qualifies
exceptions: Unless the law otherwise provides

provisions.what: Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Superintendent of Public Instruction, the Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of State, Controller, Treasurer, or Attorney General, or on the State Board of Equalization, the Governor shall nominate a person to fill the vacancy
conditions: Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Superintendent of Public Instruction, the Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of State, Controller, Treasurer, or Attorney General, or on the State Board of Equalization

provisions.what: The nominee shall take office upon confirmation by a majority of the membership of the Senate and a majority of the membership of the Assembly and shall hold office for the balance of the unexpired term
conditions: upon confirmation by a majority of the membership of the Senate and a majority of the membership of the Assembly

provisions.what: If the nominee is neither confirmed nor refused confirmation by both the Senate and the Assembly within 90 days of the submission of the nomination, the nominee shall take office as if he or she had been confirmed
conditions: In the event the nominee is neither confirmed nor refused confirmation by both the Senate and the Assembly within 90 days of the submission of the nomination
exceptions: if such 90-day period ends during a recess of the Legislature, the period shall be extended until the sixth day following the day on which the Legislature reconvenes

provisions.what: Authority may be provided by statute for the Governor to assign and reorganize functions among executive officers and agencies and their employees
conditions: Authority may be provided by statute
exceptions: other than elective officers and agencies administered by elective officers

provisions.what: The Governor is commander in chief of a militia
A militia shall be provided by statute
The Governor may call it forth to execute the law
The Governor, on conditions the Governor deems proper, may grant a reprieve, pardon, and commutation, after sentence
conditions: Subject to application procedures provided by statute
on conditions the Governor deems proper
after sentence
exceptions: except in case of impeachment

provisions.what: The Governor shall report to the Legislature each reprieve, pardon, and commutation granted, stating the pertinent facts and the reasons for granting it
The Governor may not grant a pardon or commutation to a person twice convicted of a felony
forbids: grant a pardon or commutation to a person twice convicted of a felony
exceptions: except on recommendation of the Supreme Court, 4 judges concurring

provisions.what: No decision of the parole authority with respect to the granting, denial, revocation, or suspension of parole of a person sentenced to an indeterminate term upon conviction of murder shall become effective for a period of 30 days
During the 30 days the Governor may review the decision
conditions: subject to procedures provided by statute

provisions.what: The Governor may only affirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the parole authority on the basis of the same factors which the parole authority is required to consider
The Governor shall report to the Legislature each parole decision affirmed, modified, or reversed, stating the pertinent facts and reasons for the action
The Lieutenant Governor shall have the same qualifications as the Governor
requires: the same qualifications as the Governor

provisions.what: The Lieutenant Governor is President of the Senate
The Lieutenant Governor has only a casting vote
The Lieutenant Governor shall become Governor when a vacancy occurs in the office of Governor
conditions: when a vacancy occurs in the office of Governor

provisions.what: The Lieutenant Governor shall act as Governor during the impeachment, absence from the State, or other temporary disability of the Governor or of a Governor-elect who fails to take office
conditions: during the impeachment, absence from the State, or other temporary disability of the Governor or of a Governor-elect who fails to take office

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide an order of precedence after the Lieutenant Governor for succession to the office of Governor and for the temporary exercise of the Governor’s functions
The Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction to determine all questions arising under this section
Standing to raise questions of vacancy or temporary disability is vested exclusively in a body provided by statute
The Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Controller, Secretary of State, and Treasurer shall be elected at the same time and places and for the same term as the Governor
No Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Controller, Secretary of State, or Treasurer may serve in the same office for more than 2 terms
provisions.binds: No Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Controller, Secretary of State, or Treasurer
forbids: serve in the same office for more than 2 terms

provisions.what: The Attorney General shall be the chief law officer of the State
conditions: Subject to the powers and duties of the Governor

provisions.what: It shall be the duty of the Attorney General to see that the laws of the State are uniformly and adequately enforced

The Attorney General shall have direct supervision over every district attorney and sheriff and over such other law enforcement officers as may be designated by law, in all matters pertaining to the duties of their respective offices

The Attorney General may require any of said officers to make reports concerning the investigation, detection, prosecution, and punishment of crime in their respective jurisdictions as to the Attorney General may seem advisable
It shall be the duty of the Attorney General to prosecute any violations of law of which the superior court shall have jurisdiction
conditions: Whenever in the opinion of the Attorney General any law of the State is not being adequately enforced in any county

provisions.what: In such cases the Attorney General shall have all the powers of a district attorney
The Attorney General shall assist any district attorney in the discharge of the duties of that office
conditions: When required by the public interest or directed by the Governor

provisions.what: No state officer may knowingly receive any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist or lobbying firm, as defined by the Political Reform Act of 1974, or from a person who, during the previous 12 months, has been under a contract with the state agency under the jurisdiction of the state officer
forbids: knowingly receive any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist or lobbying firm
from a person who, during the previous 12 months, has been under a contract with the state agency under the jurisdiction of the state officer

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact laws that define earned income
exceptions: earned income does not include any community property interest in the income of a spouse

provisions.what: Any state officer who knowingly receives any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist employer may not, for a period of one year following its receipt, vote upon or make, participate in making, or in any way attempt to use his or her official position to influence an action or decision before the agency for which the state officer serves which he or she knows, or has reason to know, would have a direct and significant financial impact on the lobbyist employer
provisions.binds: Any state officer who knowingly receives earned income from a lobbyist employer
conditions: would not impact the public generally or a significant segment of the public in a similar manner
exceptions: other than an action or decision involving a bill described in subdivision (c) of Section 12 of Article IV
terms: “public generally” includes an industry, trade, or profession

provisions.what: No state officer may accept any honorarium
forbids: accept any honorarium

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact laws that implement this subdivision
The Legislature shall enact laws that ban or strictly limit the acceptance of a gift by a state officer from any source if the acceptance of the gift might create a conflict of interest
No state officer may knowingly accept any compensation for appearing, agreeing to appear, or taking any other action on behalf of another person before any state government board or agency
exceptions: a state officer may engage in activities involving a board or agency which are strictly on his or her own behalf, appear in the capacity of an attorney before any court or the Workers’ Compensation Appeals Board, or act as an advocate without compensation or make an inquiry for information on behalf of a person before a board or agency

This subdivision does not prohibit any action of a partnership or firm of which the state officer is a member if the state officer does not share directly or indirectly in the fee, less any expenses attributable to that fee, resulting from that action

provisions.what: If a state officer knowingly accepts any compensation for appearing, agreeing to appear, or taking any other action on behalf of another person before any local government board or agency, the state officer may not, for one year, make, participate in making, or in any way attempt to use his or her official position to influence an action or decision before the state agency for which the state officer serves which he or she knows, or has reason to know, would have a direct and significant financial impact on that person
conditions: If a state officer knowingly accepts any compensation for appearing, agreeing to appear, or taking any other action on behalf of another person before any local government board or agency
would not impact the public generally or a significant segment of the public in a similar manner
exceptions: other than an action or decision involving a bill described in subdivision (c) of Section 12 of Article IV
terms: “public generally” includes an industry, trade, or profession

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact laws that prohibit a state officer, or a secretary of an agency or director of a department appointed by the Governor, who has not resigned or retired from state service prior to January 7, 1991, from lobbying, for compensation, before the executive branch of state government for 12 months after leaving office

“State officer,” as used in this section, means the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Controller, Insurance Commissioner, Secretary of State, Superintendent of Public Instruction, Treasurer, and member of the State Board of Equalization
terms: “State officer”: the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Controller, Insurance Commissioner, Secretary of State, Superintendent of Public Instruction, Treasurer, and member of the State Board of Equalization

provisions.what: The judicial power of this State is vested in the Supreme Court, courts of appeal, and superior courts, all of which are courts of record
provisions.holder: The Supreme Court, courts of appeal, and superior courts

provisions.what: The Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice of California and 6 associate justices
The Chief Justice may convene the court at any time
Concurrence of 4 judges present at the argument is necessary for a judgment
requires: Concurrence of 4 judges present at the argument

provisions.what: An acting Chief Justice shall perform all functions of the Chief Justice when the Chief Justice is absent or unable to act
conditions: when the Chief Justice is absent or unable to act

provisions.what: The Chief Justice or, if the Chief Justice fails to do so, the court shall select an associate justice as acting Chief Justice
provisions.binds: The Chief Justice or the court

provisions.what: The Legislature shall divide the State into districts each containing a court of appeal with one or more divisions
Each division consists of a presiding justice and 2 or more associate justices
Each division has the power of a court of appeal and shall conduct itself as a 3-judge court
Concurrence of 2 judges present at the argument is necessary for a judgment
requires: Concurrence of 2 judges present at the argument

provisions.what: An acting presiding justice shall perform all functions of the presiding justice when the presiding justice is absent or unable to act
conditions: when the presiding justice is absent or unable to act

provisions.what: The presiding justice or, if the presiding justice fails to do so, the Chief Justice shall select an associate justice of that division as acting presiding justice
provisions.binds: The presiding justice or the Chief Justice

provisions.what: In each county there is a superior court of one or more judges
The Legislature shall prescribe the number of judges and provide for the officers and employees of each superior court
The Legislature may provide that one or more judges serve more than one superior court
conditions: If the governing body of each affected county concurs

provisions.what: In each superior court there is an appellate division
The Chief Justice shall assign judges to the appellate division for specified terms pursuant to rules adopted by the Judicial Council to promote the independence of the appellate division
requires: rules, not inconsistent with statute

provisions.what: The Judicial Council consists of the Chief Justice and one other judge of the Supreme Court, three judges of courts of appeal, 10 judges of superior courts, two nonvoting court administrators, and any other nonvoting members as determined by the voting membership of the council, each appointed by the Chief Justice for a three-year term; four members of the State Bar appointed by its governing body for three-year terms; and one member of each house of the Legislature appointed as provided by the house
Council membership terminates if a member ceases to hold the position that qualified the member for appointment
conditions: if a member ceases to hold the position that qualified the member for appointment

provisions.what: A vacancy shall be filled by the appointing power for the remainder of the term
The council may appoint an Administrative Director of the Courts, who serves at its pleasure and performs functions delegated by the council or the Chief Justice
exceptions: other than adopting rules of court administration, practice and procedure

provisions.what: The council shall survey judicial business and make recommendations to the courts, make recommendations annually to the Governor and Legislature, adopt rules for court administration, practice and procedure, and perform other functions prescribed by statute
The rules adopted shall not be inconsistent with statute
The Chief Justice shall seek to expedite judicial business and to equalize the work of judges
The Chief Justice may provide for the assignment of any judge to another court
conditions: only with the judge’s consent if the court is of lower jurisdiction

provisions.what: A retired judge who consents may be assigned to any court
conditions: who consents

provisions.what: Judges shall report to the council as the Chief Justice directs concerning the condition of judicial business in their courts, cooperate with the council and hold court as assigned

The Commission on Judicial Appointments consists of the Chief Justice, the Attorney General, and the presiding justice of the court of appeal of the affected district or, if there are 2 or more presiding justices, the one who has presided longest or, when a nomination or appointment to the Supreme Court is to be considered, the presiding justice who has presided longest on any court of appeal

The Commission on Judicial Performance consists of one judge of a court of appeal and two judges of superior courts, each appointed by the Supreme Court; two members of the State Bar of California who have practiced law in this State for 10 years, each appointed by the Governor; and six citizens who are not judges, retired judges, or members of the State Bar of California, two appointed by the Governor, two by the Senate Committee on Rules, and two by the Speaker of the Assembly
All terms are for four years
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivisions (b) and (c)

provisions.what: No member shall serve more than two four-year terms, or for more than a total of 10 years if appointed to fill a vacancy
forbids: serve more than two four-year terms
for more than a total of 10 years if appointed to fill a vacancy

provisions.what: Commission membership terminates if a member ceases to hold the position that qualified the member for appointment
conditions: if a member ceases to hold the position that qualified the member for appointment

provisions.what: A vacancy shall be filled by the appointing power for the remainder of the term
A member whose term has expired may continue to serve until the vacancy has been filled by the appointing power
Appointing powers may appoint members who are already serving on the commission prior to March 1, 1995, to a single two-year term, but may not appoint them to an additional term thereafter
forbids: appoint them to an additional term thereafter

provisions.what: Two members appointed by the Supreme Court to a term commencing March 1, 1995, shall each serve a term of two years and may be reappointed to one full term
One attorney appointed by the Governor to a term commencing March 1, 1995, shall serve a term of two years and may be reappointed to one full term
One citizen member appointed by the Governor to a term commencing March 1, 1995, shall serve a term of two years and may be reappointed to one full term
One member appointed by the Senate Committee on Rules to a term commencing March 1, 1995, shall serve a term of two years and may be reappointed to one full term
One member appointed by the Speaker of the Assembly to a term commencing March 1, 1995, shall serve a term of two years and may be reappointed to one full term
All other members shall be appointed to full four-year terms commencing March 1, 1995
The State Bar of California is a public corporation
Every person admitted and licensed to practice law in this State is and shall be a member of the State Bar
exceptions: except while holding office as a judge of a court of record

provisions.what: The Supreme Court, courts of appeal, superior courts, and their judges have original jurisdiction in habeas corpus proceedings
provisions.holder: The Supreme Court, courts of appeal, superior courts, and their judges

provisions.what: Those courts also have original jurisdiction in proceedings for extraordinary relief in the nature of mandamus, certiorari, and prohibition
provisions.holder: The Supreme Court, courts of appeal, superior courts, and their judges

provisions.what: The appellate division of the superior court has original jurisdiction in proceedings for extraordinary relief in the nature of mandamus, certiorari, and prohibition directed to the superior court in causes subject to its appellate jurisdiction
provisions.holder: The appellate division of the superior court

provisions.what: Superior courts have original jurisdiction in all other causes
The court may make any comment on the evidence and the testimony and credibility of any witness as in its opinion is necessary for the proper determination of the cause
conditions: as in its opinion is necessary for the proper determination of the cause

provisions.what: The Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction when judgment of death has been pronounced
conditions: when judgment of death has been pronounced

provisions.what: Courts of appeal have appellate jurisdiction when superior courts have original jurisdiction in causes of a type within the appellate jurisdiction of the courts of appeal on June 30, 1995, and in other causes prescribed by statute
exceptions: With that exception

provisions.what: The Legislature may change the appellate jurisdiction of the courts of appeal by changing the jurisdictional amount in controversy
conditions: When appellate jurisdiction in civil causes is determined by the amount in controversy

provisions.what: The appellate division of the superior court has appellate jurisdiction in causes prescribed by statute
provisions.holder: The appellate division of the superior court
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (a)

provisions.what: The Legislature may permit courts exercising appellate jurisdiction to take evidence and make findings of fact when jury trial is waived or not a matter of right
conditions: when jury trial is waived or not a matter of right

provisions.what: The Supreme Court may, before decision, transfer to itself a cause in a court of appeal
conditions: before decision

provisions.what: It may, before decision, transfer a cause from itself to a court of appeal or from one court of appeal or division to another
conditions: before decision

provisions.what: The court to which a cause is transferred has jurisdiction
The Supreme Court may review the decision of a court of appeal in any cause

The Judicial Council shall provide, by rules of court, for the time and procedure for transfer and for review, including provisions for the time and procedure for transfer with instructions, for review of all or part of a decision, and for remand as improvidently granted
This section shall not apply to an appeal involving a judgment of death

No judgment shall be set aside, or new trial granted, in any cause, on the ground of misdirection of the jury, or of the improper admission or rejection of evidence, or for any error as to any matter of pleading, or for any error as to any matter of procedure
forbids: setting aside a judgment, or granting a new trial, on the ground of misdirection of the jury, or of the improper admission or rejection of evidence, or for any error as to any matter of pleading, or for any error as to any matter of procedure
exceptions: unless, after an examination of the entire cause, including the evidence, the court shall be of the opinion that the error complained of has resulted in a miscarriage of justice

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for the prompt publication of such opinions of the Supreme Court and courts of appeal as the Supreme Court deems appropriate
Those opinions shall be available for publication by any person
Decisions of the Supreme Court and courts of appeal that determine causes shall be in writing with reasons stated
provisions.binds: The Supreme Court and courts of appeal
requires: in writing with reasons stated

provisions.what: A person is ineligible to be a judge of a court of record unless for 10 years immediately preceding selection, the person has been a member of the State Bar or served as a judge of a court of record in this State
requires: for 10 years immediately preceding selection, the person has been a member of the State Bar or served as a judge of a court of record in this State

provisions.what: Judges of the Supreme Court shall be elected at large and judges of courts of appeal shall be elected in their districts at general elections at the same time and places as the Governor
Their terms are 12 years beginning the Monday after January 1 following their election
exceptions: except that a judge elected to an unexpired term serves the remainder of the term

provisions.what: In creating a new court of appeal district or division the Legislature shall provide that the first elective terms are 4, 8, and 12 years
conditions: In creating a new court of appeal district or division

provisions.what: Judges of superior courts shall be elected in their counties at general elections
exceptions: except as otherwise necessary to meet the requirements of federal law

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide for their election by the system prescribed in subdivision (d), or by any other arrangement
conditions: In the latter case
by two-thirds vote of the membership of each house thereof
with the advice of judges within the affected court

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide that an unopposed incumbent’s name not appear on the ballot
Terms of judges of superior courts are six years beginning the Monday after January 1 following their election
A vacancy shall be filled by election to a full term at the next general election after the second January 1 following the vacancy
The Governor shall appoint a person to fill the vacancy temporarily until the elected judge’s term begins
A judge of the Supreme Court or a court of appeal may file a declaration of candidacy to succeed to the office presently held by the judge
provisions.holder: A judge of the Supreme Court or a court of appeal
conditions: Within 30 days before August 16 preceding the expiration of the judge’s term

provisions.what: The Governor before September 16 shall nominate a candidate
conditions: If the declaration is not filed

provisions.what: At the next general election, only the candidate so declared or nominated may appear on the ballot, which shall present the question whether the candidate shall be elected
requires: The candidate shall be elected upon receiving a majority of the votes on the question

provisions.what: A candidate not elected may not be appointed to that court but later may be nominated and elected
forbids: be appointed to that court

provisions.what: The Governor shall fill vacancies in those courts by appointment
An appointee holds office until the Monday after January 1 following the first general election at which the appointee had the right to become a candidate or until an elected judge qualifies
A nomination or appointment by the Governor is effective when confirmed by the Commission on Judicial Appointments
conditions: when confirmed by the Commission on Judicial Appointments

provisions.what: Electors of a county may make this system of selection applicable to judges of superior courts
conditions: by majority of those voting
in a manner the Legislature shall provide

provisions.what: A judge of a court of record may not practice law
provisions.binds: A judge of a court of record
forbids: practice law

provisions.what: During the term for which the judge was selected a judge of a court of record is ineligible for public employment or public office other than judicial employment or judicial office
provisions.binds: A judge of a court of record
exceptions: except a judge of a court of record may accept a part-time teaching position that is outside the normal hours of his or her judicial position and that does not interfere with the regular performance of his or her judicial duties while holding office

provisions.what: A judge of a trial court of record may become eligible for election to other public office by taking a leave of absence without pay prior to filing a declaration of candidacy
requires: taking a leave of absence without pay prior to filing a declaration of candidacy

provisions.what: Acceptance of the public office is a resignation from the office of judge
A judicial officer may not receive fines or fees for personal use
forbids: receive fines or fees for personal use

provisions.what: A judicial officer may not earn retirement service credit from a public teaching position while holding judicial office
forbids: earn retirement service credit from a public teaching position while holding judicial office

provisions.what: A judge is disqualified from acting as a judge, without loss of salary, while there is pending (1) an indictment or an information charging the judge in the United States with a crime punishable as a felony under California or federal law, or (2) a petition to the Supreme Court to review a determination by the Commission on Judicial Performance to remove or retire a judge
conditions: while there is pending (1) an indictment or an information charging the judge in the United States with a crime punishable as a felony under California or federal law, or (2) a petition to the Supreme Court to review a determination by the Commission on Judicial Performance to remove or retire a judge

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance may disqualify a judge from acting as a judge, without loss of salary
conditions: upon notice of formal proceedings by the commission charging the judge with judicial misconduct or disability

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance shall suspend a judge from office without salary when in the United States the judge pleads guilty or no contest or is found guilty of a crime punishable as a felony under California or federal law or of any other crime that involves moral turpitude under that law
conditions: when in the United States the judge pleads guilty or no contest or is found guilty of a crime punishable as a felony under California or federal law or of any other crime that involves moral turpitude under that law

provisions.what: If the conviction is reversed, suspension terminates, and the judge shall be paid the salary for the judicial office held by the judge for the period of suspension
conditions: If the conviction is reversed

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance shall remove the judge from office
conditions: If the judge is suspended and the conviction becomes final

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance may retire a judge for disability that seriously interferes with the performance of the judge’s duties and is or is likely to become permanent
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (f)

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance may censure a judge or former judge or remove a judge for action occurring not more than 6 years prior to the commencement of the judge’s current term or of the former judge’s last term that constitutes willful misconduct in office, persistent failure or inability to perform the judge’s duties, habitual intemperance in the use of intoxicants or drugs, or conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice that brings the judicial office into disrepute
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (f)

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance may publicly or privately admonish a judge or former judge found to have engaged in an improper action or dereliction of duty
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (f)

provisions.what: The commission may also bar a former judge who has been censured from receiving an assignment, appointment, or reference of work from any California state court
The Supreme Court may, in its discretion, grant review of a determination by the commission to retire, remove, censure, admonish, or disqualify pursuant to subdivision (b) a judge or former judge
conditions: Upon petition by the judge or former judge

provisions.what: When the Supreme Court reviews a determination of the commission, it may make an independent review of the record
If the Supreme Court has not acted within 120 days after granting the petition, the decision of the commission shall be final
conditions: If the Supreme Court has not acted within 120 days after granting the petition

provisions.what: A judge retired by the commission shall be considered to have retired voluntarily

A judge removed by the commission is ineligible for judicial office, including receiving an assignment, appointment, or reference of work from any California state court, and pending further order of the court is suspended from practicing law in this State
provisions.binds: A judge removed by the commission

provisions.what: The State Bar may institute appropriate attorney disciplinary proceedings against any judge who retires or resigns from office with judicial disciplinary charges pending

A determination by the Commission on Judicial Performance to admonish or censure a judge or former judge of the Supreme Court or remove or retire a judge of the Supreme Court shall be reviewed by a tribunal of 7 court of appeal judges selected by lot
No court, except the Supreme Court, shall have jurisdiction in a civil action or other legal proceeding of any sort brought against the commission by a judge
provisions.binds: No court, except the Supreme Court
exceptions: except the Supreme Court

provisions.what: Any request for injunctive relief or other provisional remedy shall be granted or denied within 90 days of the filing of the request for relief
A failure to comply with the time requirements of this section does not affect the validity of commission proceedings

Members of the commission, the commission staff, and the examiners and investigators employed by the commission shall be absolutely immune from suit for all conduct at any time in the course of their official duties
provisions.holder: Members of the commission, the commission staff, and the examiners and investigators employed by the commission

provisions.what: No civil action may be maintained against a person, or adverse employment action taken against a person, by any employer, public or private, based on statements presented by the person to the commission
forbids: civil action
adverse employment action

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance shall make rules implementing this section
The commission shall make rules for the investigation of judges
The commission may provide for the confidentiality of complaints to and investigations by the commission
The commission shall make rules for formal proceedings against judges when there is cause to believe there is a disability or wrongdoing within the meaning of subdivision (d)
When the commission institutes formal proceedings, the notice of charges, the answer, and all subsequent papers and proceedings shall be open to the public
conditions: for all formal proceedings instituted after February 28, 1995

provisions.what: The commission may make explanatory statements
The budget of the commission shall be separate from the budget of any other state agency or court
The Supreme Court shall make rules for the conduct of judges, both on and off the bench, and for judicial candidates in the conduct of their campaigns
terms: "Code of Judicial Ethics": the rules the Supreme Court makes for the conduct of judges, both on and off the bench, and for judicial candidates in the conduct of their campaigns

provisions.what: The Commission on Judicial Performance shall exercise discretionary jurisdiction with regard to the oversight and discipline of subordinate judicial officers, according to the same standards, and subject to review upon petition to the Supreme Court, as specified in Section 18

No person who has been found unfit to serve as a subordinate judicial officer after a hearing before the Commission on Judicial Performance shall have the requisite status to serve as a subordinate judicial officer
provisions.binds: No person who has been found unfit to serve as a subordinate judicial officer

provisions.what: This section does not diminish or eliminate the responsibility of a court to exercise initial jurisdiction to discipline or dismiss a subordinate judicial officer as its employee

Upon request, the Commission on Judicial Performance shall provide to the Governor of any State of the Union the text of any private admonishment, advisory letter, or other disciplinary action together with any information that the Commission on Judicial Performance deems necessary to a full understanding of the commission’s action, with respect to any applicant whom the Governor of any State of the Union indicates is under consideration for any judicial appointment
conditions: Upon request

provisions.what: Upon request, the Commission on Judicial Performance shall provide the President of the United States the text of any private admonishment, advisory letter, or other disciplinary action together with any information that the Commission on Judicial Performance deems necessary to a full understanding of the commission’s action, with respect to any applicant whom the President indicates is under consideration for any federal judicial appointment
conditions: Upon request

provisions.what: Upon request, the Commission on Judicial Performance shall provide the Commission on Judicial Appointments the text of any private admonishment, advisory letter, or other disciplinary action together with any information that the Commission on Judicial Performance deems necessary to a full understanding of the commission action, with respect to any applicant whom the Commission on Judicial Appointments indicates is under consideration for any judicial appointment
conditions: Upon request

provisions.what: All information released under this section shall remain confidential and privileged
Any information released pursuant to this section shall also be provided to the applicant about whom the information was requested
provisions.holder: The applicant about whom the information was requested
exceptions: Notwithstanding subdivision (d)

provisions.what: “Private admonishment” refers to a disciplinary action against a judge by the Commission on Judicial Performance as authorized by subdivision (c) of Section 18 of Article VI, as amended November 8, 1988
terms: "Private admonishment": a disciplinary action against a judge by the Commission on Judicial Performance as authorized by subdivision (c) of Section 18 of Article VI, as amended November 8, 1988

provisions.what: The Legislature shall prescribe compensation for judges of courts of record

A judge of a court of record may not receive the salary for the judicial office held by the judge while any cause before the judge remains pending and undetermined for 90 days after it has been submitted for decision
provisions.binds: A judge of a court of record
conditions: while any cause before the judge remains pending and undetermined for 90 days after it has been submitted for decision

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for retirement, with reasonable allowance, of judges of courts of record for age or disability
The court may order a cause to be tried by a temporary judge who is a member of the State Bar, sworn and empowered to act until final determination of the cause
requires: who is a member of the State Bar
sworn
conditions: On stipulation of the parties litigant

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide for the appointment by trial courts of record of officers such as commissioners to perform subordinate judicial duties
The civil service includes every officer and employee of the State
exceptions: except as otherwise provided in this Constitution

provisions.what: In the civil service permanent appointment and promotion shall be made under a general system based on merit ascertained by competitive examination
requires: a general system based on merit ascertained by competitive examination

provisions.what: There is a Personnel Board of 5 members appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate, a majority of the membership concurring, for 10-year terms and until their successors are appointed and qualified
Appointment to fill a vacancy is for the unexpired portion of the term
A member may be removed by concurrent resolution adopted by each house
conditions: two-thirds of the membership of each house concurring

provisions.what: The board annually shall elect one of its members as presiding officer
The board shall appoint and prescribe compensation for an executive officer who shall be a member of the civil service but not a member of the board
requires: who shall be a member of the civil service but not a member of the board

provisions.what: The board shall enforce the civil service statutes
The board shall prescribe probationary periods and classifications, adopt other rules authorized by statute, and review disciplinary actions
conditions: by majority vote of all its members

provisions.what: The executive officer shall administer the civil service statutes under rules of the board
Exempt from civil service: Officers and employees appointed or employed by the Legislature, either house, or legislative committees
Exempt from civil service: Officers and employees appointed or employed by councils, commissions or public corporations in the judicial branch or by a court of record or officer thereof
Exempt from civil service: Officers elected by the people and a deputy and an employee selected by each elected officer
Exempt from civil service: Members of boards and commissions
Exempt from civil service: A deputy or employee selected by each board or commission either appointed by the Governor or authorized by statute

Exempt from civil service: State officers directly appointed by the Governor with or without the consent or confirmation of the Senate and the employees of the Governor’s office, and the employees of the Lieutenant Governor’s office directly appointed or employed by the Lieutenant Governor
Exempt from civil service: A deputy or employee selected by each officer, except members of boards and commissions, exempted under Section 4(f)
Exempt from civil service: Officers and employees of the University of California and the California State Colleges
Exempt from civil service: The teaching staff of schools under the jurisdiction of the Department of Education or the Superintendent of Public Instruction
Exempt from civil service: Member, inmate, and patient help in state homes, charitable or correctional institutions, and state facilities for mentally ill or retarded persons
Exempt from civil service: Members of the militia while engaged in military service
Exempt from civil service: Officers and employees of district agricultural associations employed less than 6 months in a calendar year
The Attorney General may appoint or employ six deputies or employees
conditions: In addition to positions exempted by other provisions of this section

provisions.what: The Public Utilities Commission may appoint or employ one deputy or employee
conditions: In addition to positions exempted by other provisions of this section

provisions.what: The Legislative Counsel may appoint or employ two deputies or employees
conditions: In addition to positions exempted by other provisions of this section

provisions.what: A temporary appointment may be made to a position for which there is no employment list
conditions: for which there is no employment list

provisions.what: No person may serve in one or more positions under temporary appointment longer than 9 months in 12 consecutive months
forbids: serve in one or more positions under temporary appointment longer than 9 months in 12 consecutive months

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide preferences for veterans and their surviving spouses
The board by special rule may permit persons in exempt positions, brought under civil service by constitutional provision, to qualify to continue in their positions
conditions: by special rule

provisions.what: The board by special rule shall provide for persons who previously performed this work to qualify to continue in their positions in the state civil service
requires: subject to such minimum standards as may be established by statute
conditions: When the State undertakes work previously performed by a county, city, public district of this State or by a federal department or agency

provisions.what: A person holding a lucrative office under the United States or other power may not hold a civil office of profit
provisions.binds: A person holding a lucrative office under the United States or other power
forbids: hold a civil office of profit

provisions.what: A local officer or postmaster whose compensation does not exceed 500 dollars per year or an officer in the militia or a member of a reserve component of the armed forces of the United States is not a holder of a lucrative office, nor is the holding of a civil office of profit affected by this military service
exceptions: except where on active federal duty for more than 30 days in any year

provisions.what: Every person shall be disqualified from holding any office of profit in this State who shall have been convicted of having given or offered a bribe to procure personal election or appointment
provisions.binds: Every person who shall have been convicted of having given or offered a bribe to procure personal election or appointment
forbids: holding any office of profit in this State

provisions.what: Laws shall be made to exclude persons convicted of bribery, perjury, forgery, malfeasance in office, or other high crimes from office or serving on juries

The privilege of free suffrage shall be supported by laws regulating elections and prohibiting, under adequate penalties, all undue influence thereon from power, bribery, tumult, or other improper practice
requires: laws regulating elections and prohibiting, under adequate penalties, all undue influence thereon from power, bribery, tumult, or other improper practice

provisions.what: No person or organization which advocates the overthrow of the Government of the United States or the State by force or violence or other unlawful means or who advocates the support of a foreign government against the United States in the event of hostilities shall hold any office or employment under this State, including but not limited to the University of California, or with any county, city or county, city, district, political subdivision, authority, board, bureau, commission or other public agency of this State
provisions.binds: No person or organization which advocates the overthrow of the Government of the United States or the State by force or violence or other unlawful means or who advocates the support of a foreign government against the United States in the event of hostilities
forbids: Hold any office or employment under this State
conditions: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Constitution

provisions.what: No person or organization which advocates the overthrow of the Government of the United States or the State by force or violence or other unlawful means or who advocates the support of a foreign government against the United States in the event of hostilities shall receive any exemption from any tax imposed by this State or any county, city or county, city, district, political subdivision, authority, board, bureau, commission or other public agency of this State
provisions.binds: No person or organization which advocates the overthrow of the Government of the United States or the State by force or violence or other unlawful means or who advocates the support of a foreign government against the United States in the event of hostilities
forbids: Receive any exemption from any tax
conditions: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Constitution

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact such laws as may be necessary to enforce the provisions of this section

No person who is found liable in a civil action for making libelous or slanderous statements against an opposing candidate during the course of an election campaign for any federal, statewide, Board of Equalization, or legislative office or for any county, city and county, city, district, or any other local elective office shall retain the seat to which he or she is elected
provisions.binds: No person found liable for libelous or slanderous statements against an opposing candidate
forbids: retain the seat to which he or she is elected
conditions: where it is established that the libel or slander was a major contributing cause in the defeat of an opposing candidate

provisions.what: A libelous or slanderous statement shall be deemed to have been made by a person if that person actually made the statement or if the person actually or constructively assented to, authorized, or ratified the statement
terms: "made by a person": that person actually made the statement or actually or constructively assented to, authorized, or ratified the statement

provisions.what: “Federal office” means the office of United States Senator and Member of the House of Representatives; it is intended that candidates seeking those offices comply with this section
conditions: to the extent that the provisions of this section do not conflict with any provision of federal law
terms: "Federal office": the office of United States Senator and Member of the House of Representatives

provisions.what: The trier of fact shall make a separate, distinct finding on whether libelous or slanderous statements were a major contributing cause in the defeat of an opposing candidate
The person holding office shall be disqualified from or shall forfeit that office as provided in subdivision (d)
conditions: If the trier of fact finds that libel or slander was a major contributing cause in the defeat of an opposing candidate and that the libelous or slanderous statement was made with knowledge that it was false or with reckless disregard of whether it was false or true

provisions.what: The findings required by this section shall be in writing and shall be incorporated as part of the judgment
requires: in writing
incorporated as part of the judgment

provisions.what: Disqualification or forfeiture shall create a vacancy in office, which shall be filled in the manner provided by law for the filling of a vacancy in that particular office
The person shall be disqualified from or shall forfeit the office involved in that election and shall have no authority to exercise the powers or perform the duties of the office
conditions: Once the judgment of liability is entered by the trial court and the time for filing a notice of appeal has expired, or all possibility of direct attack in the courts of this State has been finally exhausted

provisions.what: This section shall apply to libelous or slanderous statements made on or after the effective date of this section

The Legislators’ Retirement System shall not pay any unmodified retirement allowance or its actuarial equivalent to any person who on or after January 1, 1987, entered for the first time any state office for which membership in the Legislators’ Retirement System was elective or to any beneficiary or survivor of such a person, which exceeds the higher of (1) the salary receivable by the person currently serving in the office or (2) the highest salary received by the retired person while serving in that office
forbids: pay any unmodified retirement allowance or its actuarial equivalent which exceeds the higher of (1) the salary receivable by the person currently serving in the office in which the retired person served or (2) the highest salary that was received by the retired person while serving in that office

provisions.what: The Judges’ Retirement System shall not pay any unmodified retirement allowance or its actuarial equivalent to any person who on or after January 1, 1987, entered for the first time any judicial office subject to the Judges’ Retirement System or to any beneficiary or survivor of such a person, which exceeds the higher of (1) the salary receivable by the person currently serving in the judicial office or (2) the highest salary received by the retired person while serving in that judicial office
forbids: pay any unmodified retirement allowance or its actuarial equivalent which exceeds the higher of (1) the salary receivable by the person currently serving in the judicial office in which the retired person served or (2) the highest salary that was received by the retired person while serving in that judicial office

provisions.what: The Legislature may define the terms used in this section

If any part of this measure or the application to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications which reasonably can be given effect without the invalid provision or application
The Legislature shall encourage by all suitable means the promotion of intellectual, scientific, moral, and agricultural improvement
A Superintendent of Public Instruction shall be elected by the qualified electors of the State at each gubernatorial election
The Superintendent of Public Instruction shall enter upon the duties of the office on the first Monday after the first day of January next succeeding each gubernatorial election
No Superintendent of Public Instruction may serve more than 2 terms
forbids: serve more than 2 terms

provisions.what: The State Board of Education shall appoint one Deputy Superintendent of Public Instruction and three Associate Superintendents of Public Instruction
conditions: on nomination of the Superintendent of Public Instruction

provisions.what: The Deputy and Associate Superintendents shall be exempt from state civil service and their terms of office shall be four years
This section shall not be construed as prohibiting the appointment, in accordance with law, of additional Associate Superintendents of Public Instruction subject to state civil service
A Superintendent of Schools for each county may be elected by the qualified electors thereof at each gubernatorial election or may be appointed by the county board of education
The manner of the selection shall be determined by a majority vote of the electors of the county voting on the question
Two or more counties may unite for the purpose of electing or appointing one joint superintendent for the counties so uniting
conditions: by an election conducted pursuant to Section 3.2 of this article

provisions.what: The Legislature shall prescribe the qualifications required of county superintendents of schools, and for these purposes shall classify the several counties in the State
conditions: Notwithstanding any provision of this Constitution to the contrary

provisions.what: The county board of education or joint county board of education shall fix the salary of the county superintendent of schools or the joint county superintendent of schools
provisions.holder: The county board of education or joint county board of education
conditions: Notwithstanding any provision of this Constitution to the contrary

provisions.what: Any two or more chartered counties, or nonchartered counties, or any combination thereof, may establish one joint board of education and one joint county superintendent of schools for the counties so uniting
provisions.holder: Any two or more chartered counties, or nonchartered counties, or any combination thereof
conditions: by a majority vote of the electors of each such county voting on the proposition at an election called for that purpose in each such county
Notwithstanding any provision of this Constitution to the contrary

provisions.what: A joint county board of education and a joint county superintendent of schools shall be governed by the general statutes and shall not be governed by the provisions of any county charter
requires: governed by the general statutes
forbids: governed by the provisions of any county charter

provisions.what: It shall be competent to provide in any charter framed for a county, or by the amendment of any such charter, for the election of the members of the county board of education of such county and for their qualifications and terms of office
exceptions: Except as provided in Section 3.2 of this article

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for a system of common schools by which a free school shall be kept up and supported in each district at least six months in every year
requires: a free school shall be kept up and supported in each district at least six months in every year
conditions: after the first year in which a school has been established

provisions.what: Each person employed by a school district as a teacher or in any other position requiring certification qualifications shall be paid a salary at the rate of an annual salary of not less than twenty-four hundred dollars ($2,400) for a person serving full time, as defined by law
provisions.holder: Each person employed by a school district as a teacher or in any other position requiring certification qualifications
exceptions: other than a substitute employee

provisions.what: The Public School System shall include all kindergarten schools, elementary schools, secondary schools, technical schools, and state colleges, established in accordance with law and the school districts and the other agencies authorized to maintain them

No school or college or any other part of the Public School System shall be, directly or indirectly, transferred from the Public School System or placed under the jurisdiction of any authority other than one included within the Public School System
forbids: transferred from the Public School System
placed under the jurisdiction of any authority other than one included within the Public School System

provisions.what: The Legislature shall add to the State School Fund such other means from the revenues of the State as shall provide for apportionment in each fiscal year an amount not less than one hundred eighty dollars ($180) per pupil in average daily attendance in the kindergarten, elementary, secondary, and technical schools during the next preceding fiscal year

The entire State School Fund shall be apportioned in each fiscal year in such manner as the Legislature may provide, through the school districts and other agencies maintaining such schools, for the support of, and aid to, kindergarten schools, elementary schools, secondary schools, and technical schools
requires: there shall be apportioned to each school district in each fiscal year not less than one hundred twenty dollars ($120) per pupil in average daily attendance in the district during the next preceding fiscal year
the amount apportioned to each school district in each fiscal year shall be not less than twenty-four hundred dollars ($2,400)

provisions.what: Solely with respect to any county or city and county charter retirement system in which certificated school employees' contributions and benefits are based on the proportion of their salaries contributed by the county or city and county, all amounts apportioned under this section shall be considered as though derived from county or city and county school taxes and not money provided by the State
Nothing in this constitution shall forbid the formation of districts for school purposes situate in more than one county or the issuance of bonds by such districts
conditions: under such general laws as have been or may hereafter be prescribed by the legislature

provisions.what: The officers mentioned in such laws shall be authorized to levy and assess such taxes and perform all such other acts as may be prescribed therein for the purpose of paying such bonds and carrying out the other powers conferred upon such districts
provisions.holder: The officers mentioned in such laws

provisions.what: All such bonds shall be issued subject to the limitations prescribed in section eighteen of article eleven
requires: subject to the limitations prescribed in section eighteen of article eleven hereof

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for the appointment or election of the State Board of Education and a board of education in each county or for the election of a joint county board of education for two or more counties
The State Board of Education shall adopt textbooks for use in grades one through eight throughout the State, to be furnished without cost as provided by statute
requires: to be furnished without cost as provided by statute

provisions.what: No public money shall ever be appropriated for the support of any sectarian or denominational school, or any school not under the exclusive control of the officers of the public schools
forbids: appropriating public money for the support of any sectarian or denominational school, or any school not under the exclusive control of the officers of the public schools

provisions.what: Nor shall any sectarian or denominational doctrine be taught, or instruction thereon be permitted, directly or indirectly, in any of the common schools of this State
forbids: teaching sectarian or denominational doctrine in the common schools
permitting instruction thereon, directly or indirectly

provisions.what: The University of California shall constitute a public trust, to be administered by the existing corporation known as “The Regents of the University of California,” with full powers of organization and government
provisions.holder: The Regents of the University of California
exceptions: subject only to such legislative control as may be necessary to insure the security of its funds and compliance with the terms of the endowments of the university and such competitive bidding procedures as may be made applicable to the university by statute for the letting of construction contracts, sales of real property, and purchasing of materials, goods, and services

provisions.what: Said corporation shall be in form a board composed of seven ex officio members: the Governor, the Lieutenant Governor, the Speaker of the Assembly, the Superintendent of Public Instruction, the president and the vice president of the alumni association of the university and the acting president of the university, and 18 appointive members
exceptions: the present appointive members shall hold office until the expiration of their present terms

provisions.what: The 18 appointive members are appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate
conditions: approved by the Senate, a majority of the membership concurring

provisions.what: The terms of the members appointed prior to November 5, 1974, shall be 16 years; the terms of members appointed for terms commencing on and after March 1, 1976, shall be 12 years; two members shall be appointed for terms commencing on March 1, 1976, and on March 1 of each year thereafter

No such appointments shall be made for terms to commence on March 1, 1979, or on March 1 of each fourth year thereafter, to the end that no appointment to the regents for a newly commencing term shall be made during the first year of any gubernatorial term of office
forbids: appointments for terms to commence on March 1, 1979, or on March 1 of each fourth year thereafter

provisions.what: During the period of transition until the appointive membership is comprised exclusively of persons serving for terms of 12 years, the total number of appointive members may exceed the numbers specified in the preceeding paragraph
In case of any vacancy, the appointee to fill such vacancy shall be appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate, for the balance of the term for which such vacancy exists
conditions: approved by the Senate, a majority of the membership concurring

provisions.what: The members of the board may, in their discretion, appoint to the board either or both of the following persons as members with all rights of participation: a member of the faculty at a campus of the university or of another institution of higher education; a person enrolled as a student at a campus of the university for each regular academic term during his service as a member of the board
conditions: following procedures established by them and after consultation with representatives of faculty and students of the university, including appropriate officers of the academic senate and student governments

provisions.what: Any person so appointed shall serve for not less than one year commencing on July 1

Regents shall be able persons broadly reflective of the economic, cultural, and social diversity of the State, including ethnic minorities and women; it is not intended that formulas or specific ratios be applied in the selection of regents

In the selection of the Regents, the Governor shall consult an advisory committee composed of the Speaker of the Assembly and two public members appointed by the Speaker, the President Pro Tempore of the Senate and two public members appointed by the Rules Committee of the Senate, two public members appointed by the Governor, the chairman of the regents, an alumnus chosen by the alumni association, a student chosen by the Council of Student Body Presidents, and a faculty member chosen by the academic senate

Public members shall serve for four years, except that one each of the initially appointed members selected by the Speaker of the Assembly, the President Pro Tempore of the Senate, and the Governor shall be appointed to serve for two years; student, alumni, and faculty members shall serve for one year
Student, alumni, and faculty members may not be regents of the university at the time of their service on the advisory committee
provisions.binds: Student, alumni, and faculty members of the advisory committee

provisions.what: The Regents shall be vested with the legal title and the management and disposition of the property of the university and of property held for its benefit and shall have the power to take and hold, either by purchase or by donation, or gift, testamentary or otherwise, or in any other manner, without restriction, all real and personal property for the benefit of the university or incidentally to its conduct
provisions.holder: The Regents of the University of California
exceptions: sales of university real property shall be subject to such competitive bidding procedures as may be provided by statute

provisions.what: Said corporation shall also have all the powers necessary or convenient for the effective administration of its trust, including the power to sue and to be sued, to use a seal, and to delegate to its committees or to the faculty of the university, or to others, such authority or functions as it may deem wise
provisions.holder: The Regents of the University of California

provisions.what: The Regents shall receive all funds derived from the sale of lands pursuant to the act of Congress of July 2, 1862, and any subsequent acts amendatory thereof
The university shall be entirely independent of all political or sectarian influence and kept free therefrom in the appointment of its regents and in the administration of its affairs
forbids: political or sectarian influence in the appointment of its regents and in the administration of its affairs

provisions.what: No person shall be debarred admission to any department of the university on account of race, religion, ethnic heritage, or sex
forbids: debarring admission on account of race, religion, ethnic heritage, or sex

provisions.what: Meetings of the Regents of the University of California shall be public
exceptions: with exceptions and notice requirements as may be provided by statute

provisions.what: The Legislature shall have power, by general law, to provide for the incorporation and organization of school districts, high school districts, and community college districts, of every kind and class
The Legislature may classify such districts

The Legislature may authorize the governing boards of all school districts to initiate and carry on any programs, activities, or to otherwise act in any manner which is not in conflict with the laws and purposes for which school districts are established
conditions: not in conflict with the laws and purposes for which school districts are established

provisions.what: It shall be competent, in all charters framed under the authority given by Section 5 of Article XI, to provide for the manner in which, the times at which, and the terms for which the members of boards of education shall be elected or appointed, for their qualifications, compensation and removal, and for the number which shall constitute any one of such boards
conditions: in addition to those provisions allowable by this Constitution, and by the laws of the State

provisions.what: No charter amendment effecting a change in the manner in which, the times at which, or the terms for which the members of the board of education shall be elected or appointed, for their qualifications, compensation, or removal, or for the number which shall constitute such board, shall be adopted unless it is submitted to and approved by a majority of all the qualified electors of the school district or community college district voting on the question
requires: submitted to and approved by a majority of all the qualified electors of the school district or community college district voting on the question
conditions: when the boundaries of a school district or community college district extend beyond the limits of a city whose charter provides for any or all of the foregoing with respect to the members of its board of education
Notwithstanding Section 3 of Article XI

provisions.what: Any such amendment, and any portion of a proposed charter or a revised charter which would establish or change any of the foregoing provisions respecting a board of education, shall be submitted to the electors of the school district or community college district as one or more separate questions
The failure of any such separate question to be approved shall have the result of continuing in effect the applicable existing law with respect to that board of education
The right of eminent domain is hereby declared to exist in the State to all frontages on the navigable waters of this State

The general welfare requires that the water resources of the State be put to beneficial use to the fullest extent of which they are capable, that the waste or unreasonable use or unreasonable method of use of water be prevented, and that the conservation of such waters is to be exercised with a view to the reasonable and beneficial use thereof in the interest of the people and for the public welfare
conditions: because of the conditions prevailing in this State

provisions.what: The right to water or to the use or flow of water in or from any natural stream or water course in this State is and shall be limited to such water as shall be reasonably required for the beneficial use to be served, and such right does not and shall not extend to the waste or unreasonable use or unreasonable method of use or unreasonable method of diversion of water
forbids: the waste or unreasonable use or unreasonable method of use or unreasonable method of diversion of water

provisions.what: Riparian rights in a stream or water course attach to, but to no more than so much of the flow thereof as may be required or used consistently with this section, for the purposes for which such lands are, or may be made adaptable, in view of such reasonable and beneficial uses

Nothing herein shall be construed as depriving any riparian owner of the reasonable use of water of the stream to which the owner’s land is riparian under reasonable methods of diversion and use, or as depriving any appropriator of water to which the appropriator is lawfully entitled
This section shall be self-executing
The Legislature may also enact laws in the furtherance of the policy in this section contained

All tidelands within two miles of any incorporated city, city and county, or town in this State, and fronting on the water of any harbor, estuary, bay, or inlet used for the purposes of navigation, shall be withheld from grant or sale to private persons, partnerships, or corporations
forbids: grant or sale to private persons, partnerships, or corporations
exceptions: any such tidelands, reserved to the State solely for street purposes, which the Legislature finds and declares are not used for navigation purposes and are not necessary for such purposes may be sold

provisions.what: Any such tidelands, reserved to the State solely for street purposes, which the Legislature finds and declares are not used for navigation purposes and are not necessary for such purposes may be sold to any town, city, county, city and county, municipal corporations, private persons, partnerships or corporations
conditions: which the Legislature finds and declares are not used for navigation purposes and are not necessary for such purposes
subject to such conditions as the Legislature determines are necessary to be imposed in connection with any such sales in order to protect the public interest

provisions.what: No individual, partnership, or corporation, claiming or possessing the frontage or tidal lands of a harbor, bay, inlet, estuary, or other navigable water in this State, shall be permitted to exclude the right of way to such water whenever it is required for any public purpose, nor to destroy or obstruct the free navigation of such water
provisions.binds: No individual, partnership, or corporation, claiming or possessing the frontage or tidal lands of a harbor, bay, inlet, estuary, or other navigable water in this State
forbids: exclude the right of way to such water whenever it is required for any public purpose
destroy or obstruct the free navigation of such water

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact such laws as will give the most liberal construction to this provision, so that access to the navigable waters of this State shall be always attainable for the people thereof
requires: enact such laws as will give the most liberal construction to this provision

provisions.what: The use of all water now appropriated, or that may hereafter be appropriated, for sale, rental, or distribution, is hereby declared to be a public use

The use of all water now appropriated, or that may hereafter be appropriated, for sale, rental, or distribution, is subject to the regulation and control of the State, in the manner to be prescribed by law
conditions: in the manner to be prescribed by law

provisions.what: The right to collect rates or compensation for the use of water supplied to any county, city and county, or town, or the inhabitants thereof, is a franchise, and cannot be exercised except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law
requires: by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law
forbids: exercising the right to collect rates or compensation for the use of water except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law

provisions.what: The acceptance of the interest shall constitute an agreement by the agency to conform to the laws of California as to the acquisition, control, use, and distribution of water with respect to the land so acquired
provisions.binds: Any agency of government, local, state, or federal
requires: conform to the laws of California as to the acquisition, control, use, and distribution of water with respect to the land so acquired
conditions: Whenever any agency of government, local, state, or federal, hereafter acquires any interest in real property in this State

provisions.what: The people of the State hereby provide the following guarantees and protections in this article for water rights, water quality, and fish and wildlife resources

No statute amending or repealing, or adding to, the provisions of the statute enacted by Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature which specify (1) the manner in which the State will protect fish and wildlife resources in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and San Francisco Bay system westerly of the delta; (2) the manner in which the State will protect existing water rights in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta; and (3) the manner in which the State will operate the State Water Resources Development System to comply with water quality standards and water quality control plans, shall become effective unless approved by the electors
requires: approved by the electors in the same manner as statutes amending initiative statutes are approved
exceptions: the Legislature may, by statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

provisions.what: The Legislature may, by statute, amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions
requires: statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring
conditions: if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

provisions.what: No water shall be available for appropriation by storage in, or by direct diversion from, any of the components of the California Wild and Scenic Rivers System, as such system exists on January 1, 1981, where such appropriation is for export of water into another major hydrologic basin of the State
conditions: where such appropriation is for export of water into another major hydrologic basin of the State, as defined in the Department of Water Resources Bulletin 160-74
exceptions: unless such export is expressly authorized prior to such appropriation by: (a) an initiative statute approved by the electors, or (b) the Legislature, by statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring

provisions.what: No statute amending or repealing, or adding to, the provisions of Part 4.5 (commencing with Section 12200) of Division 6 of the Water Code (the Delta Protection Act) shall become effective unless approved by the electors
requires: approved by the electors in the same manner as statutes amending initiative statutes are approved
exceptions: the Legislature may, by statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

provisions.what: The Legislature may, by statute, amend or repeal, or add to, the provisions of the Delta Protection Act
requires: statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring
conditions: if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

provisions.what: No public agency may utilize eminent domain proceedings to acquire water rights, which are held for uses within the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta as defined in Section 12220 of the Water Code, or any contract rights for water or water quality maintenance in the Delta for the purpose of exporting such water from the Delta
forbids: utilize eminent domain proceedings to acquire water rights, which are held for uses within the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, or any contract rights for water or water quality maintenance in the Delta
conditions: for the purpose of exporting such water from the Delta
