exceptions: This provision shall not be construed to prohibit the utilization of eminent domain proceedings for the purpose of acquiring land or any other rights necessary for the construction of water facilities, including, but not limited to, facilities authorized in Chapter 8 (commencing with Section 12930) of Part 6 of Division 6 of the Water Code

provisions.what: The venue of any of the following actions or proceedings brought in a superior court shall be Sacramento County: (1) an action or proceeding to attack, review, set aside, void, or annul any provision of the statute enacted by Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session; (2) to attack, review, set aside, void, or annul the determination made by the Director of Water Resources and the Director of Fish and Game pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 11255 of the Water Code; (3) which would have the effect of attacking, reviewing, preventing, or substantially delaying the construction, operation, or maintenance of the peripheral canal unit; (4) to require the State Water Resources Development System to comply with subdivision (b) of Section 11460 of the Water Code; (5) to require the Department of Water Resources or its successor agency to comply with the permanent agreement specified in subdivision (a) of Section 11256 of the Water Code; (6) to require the Department of Water Resources or its successor agency to comply with the provisions of the contracts entered into pursuant to Section 11456 of the Water Code

An action or proceeding described in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) shall be commenced within one year after the effective date of the statute enacted by Senate Bill No. 200. Any other action or proceeding described in subdivision (a) shall be commenced within one year after the cause of action arises
exceptions: unless a shorter period is otherwise provided by statute

provisions.what: The superior court or a court of appeals shall give preference to the actions or proceedings described in this section over all civil actions or proceedings pending in the court. The superior court shall commence hearing any such action or proceeding within six months after the commencement of the action or proceeding
provisions.binds: The superior court or a court of appeals
requires: give preference to the actions or proceedings described in this section over all civil actions or proceedings pending in the court
commence hearing any such action or proceeding within six months after the commencement of the action or proceeding
exceptions: any such hearing may be delayed by joint stipulation of the parties or at the discretion of the court for good cause shown

provisions.what: The provisions of this section shall supersede any provisions of law requiring courts to give preference to other civil actions or proceedings. The provisions of this subdivision may be enforced by mandamus

The Supreme Court shall, upon the request of any party, transfer to itself, before a decision in the court of appeal, any appeal or petition for extraordinary relief from an action or proceeding described in this section. The request for transfer shall receive preference on the Supreme Court’s calendar. If the action or proceeding is transferred to the Supreme Court, the Supreme Court shall commence to hear the matter within six months of the transfer
conditions: upon the request of any party
exceptions: unless the Supreme Court determines that the action or proceeding is unlikely to substantially affect (1) the construction, operation, or maintenance of the peripheral canal unit described in subdivision (a) of Section 11255 of the Water Code, (2) compliance with subdivision (b) of Section 11460 of the Water Code, (3) compliance with the permanent agreement specified in Section 11256 of the Water Code, or (4) compliance with the provisions of the contracts entered into pursuant to Section 11456 of the Water Code
unless the parties by joint stipulation request additional time or the court, for good cause shown, grants additional time

provisions.what: The remedy prescribed by the court for an action or proceeding described in paragraph (4), (5), or (6) of subdivision (a) shall include, but need not be limited to, compliance with subdivision (b) of Section 11460 of the Water Code, the permanent agreement specified in Section 11256 of the Water Code, or the provisions of the contracts entered into pursuant to Section 11456 of the Water Code
The Board of Supervisors of the County of Sacramento may apply to the State Board of Control for actual costs imposed by the requirements of this section upon the county
provisions.holder: The Board of Supervisors of the County of Sacramento

provisions.what: The State Board of Control shall pay such actual costs
Nothing in this Article shall be construed as prohibiting the Supreme Court from exercising the transfer authority contained in Article VI, Section 12 of the Constitution
conditions: Notwithstanding the provisions of this section

provisions.what: State agencies shall exercise their authorized powers in a manner consistent with the protections provided by this article
requires: exercise their authorized powers in a manner consistent with the protections provided by this article

provisions.what: This article shall have no force or effect unless Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature is enacted and takes effect
conditions: unless Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature is enacted and takes effect

provisions.what: This article shall be known and may be cited as the Marine Resources Protection Act of 1990
“District” means a fish and game district as defined in the Fish and Game Code by statute on January 1, 1990
terms: "District": a fish and game district as defined in the Fish and Game Code by statute on January 1, 1990

provisions.what: All references to Fish and Game Code sections, articles, chapters, parts, and divisions are defined as those statutes in effect on January 1, 1990
exceptions: Except as specifically provided in this article

provisions.what: “Ocean waters” means the waters of the Pacific Ocean regulated by the State
terms: "Ocean waters": the waters of the Pacific Ocean regulated by the State

provisions.what: “Zone” means the Marine Resources Protection zone established pursuant to this article, consisting of: (1) waters less than 70 fathoms or within one mile, whichever is less, around the Channel Islands of San Miguel, Santa Rosa, Santa Cruz, Anacapa, San Nicolaus, Santa Barbara, Santa Catalina, and San Clemente; (2) the area within three nautical miles offshore of the mainland coast, and within three nautical miles off any manmade breakwater, between a line extending due west from Point Arguello and a line extending due west from the Mexican border; (3) waters less than 35 fathoms between a line running 180 degrees true from Point Fermin and a line running 270 degrees true from the south jetty of Newport Harbor
terms: "Zone": the Marine Resources Protection zone established pursuant to this article, consisting of the waters around the Channel Islands, the area off the mainland coast between Point Arguello and the Mexican border, and the waters between Point Fermin and Newport Harbor described in paragraphs (1) to (3)

provisions.what: From January 1, 1991, to December 31, 1993, inclusive, gill nets or trammel nets may only be used in the zone pursuant to a nontransferable permit issued by the Department of Fish and Game pursuant to Section 5
requires: a nontransferable permit issued by the Department of Fish and Game pursuant to Section 5
conditions: From January 1, 1991, to December 31, 1993, inclusive

provisions.what: On and after January 1, 1994, gill nets and trammel nets shall not be used in the zone
forbids: using gill nets and trammel nets in the zone
conditions: On and after January 1, 1994

provisions.what: Gill nets and trammel nets may not be used to take any species of rockfish
forbids: using gill nets and trammel nets to take any species of rockfish
conditions: Notwithstanding any other provision of law

provisions.what: In ocean waters north of Point Arguello on and after the effective date of this article, the use of gill nets and trammel nets shall be regulated by the provisions of Article 4, Article 5 and Article 6 of Chapter 3 of Part 3 of Division 6 of the Fish and Game Code, or any regulation or order issued pursuant to these articles, in effect on January 1, 1990
exceptions: as to Sections 8680, 8681, 8681.7, and 8682, and subdivisions (a) through (f), inclusive of Section 8681.5 of the Fish and Game Code, or any regulation or order issued pursuant to these sections, the provisions in effect on January 1, 1989, shall control where not in conflict with other provisions of this article, and shall be applicable to all ocean waters

provisions.what: The Legislature shall not be precluded from imposing more restrictions on the use and/or possession of gill nets or trammel nets
conditions: Notwithstanding the provisions of this section

provisions.what: The Director of the Department of Fish and Game shall not authorize the use of gill nets or trammel nets in any area where the use is not permitted even if the director makes specified findings
provisions.binds: The Director of the Department of Fish and Game
forbids: authorize the use of gill nets or trammel nets in any area where the use is not permitted

provisions.what: The Department of Fish and Game shall issue a permit to use a gill net or trammel net in the zone for the period specified in subdivision (a) of Section 3 to any applicant who meets both of the following requirements
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game
requires: (a) Has a commercial fishing license issued pursuant to Sections 7850–7852.3 of the Fish and Game Code
(b) Has a permit issued pursuant to Section 8681 of the Fish and Game Code and is presently the owner or operator of a vessel equipped with a gill net or trammel net

provisions.what: The Department of Fish and Game shall charge the following fees for permits issued pursuant to Section 5: 1991, $250; 1992, 500; 1993, 1,000
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game

provisions.what: Within 90 days after the effective date of this section, every person who intends to seek the compensation provided in subdivision (b) shall notify the Department of Fish and Game, on forms provided by the department, of that intent
provisions.binds: Every person who intends to seek the compensation provided in subdivision (b)

provisions.what: Any person who does not submit the form within that 90-day period shall not be compensated pursuant to subdivision (b)
conditions: does not submit the form within that 90-day period

provisions.what: The department shall publish a list of all persons submitting the form within 120 days after the effective date of this section
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game

provisions.what: Any person who holds a permit issued pursuant to Section 5 and operates in the zone may surrender that permit to the department and agree to permanently discontinue fishing with gill or trammel nets in the zone, for which he or she shall receive a one time compensation which shall be based upon the average annual ex vessel value of the fish other than any species of rockfish landed by a fisherman, taken pursuant to a valid general gill net or trammel net permit within the zone during the years 1983 to 1987, inclusive
provisions.holder: Any person who holds a permit issued pursuant to Section 5 and operates in the zone
requires: surrender that permit to the department
agree to permanently discontinue fishing with gill or trammel nets in the zone
conditions: After July 1, 1993, and before January 1, 1994

provisions.what: The department shall verify those landings by reviewing logs and landing receipts submitted to it
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game

provisions.what: Any person who is denied compensation by the department as a result of the department’s failure to verify landings may appeal that decision to the Fish and Game Commission
provisions.holder: Any person who is denied compensation by the department as a result of the department’s failure to verify landings

provisions.what: The State Board of Control shall, prior to the disbursement of any funds, verify the eligibility of each person seeking compensation and the amount of the compensation to be provided in order to ensure compliance with this section
No compensation shall be paid under this article
conditions: Unless the Legislature enacts any required enabling legislation to implement this section on or before July 1, 1993

provisions.what: There is hereby created the Marine Resources Protection Account in the Fish and Game Preservation Fund
On and after January 1, 1991, the Department of Fish and Game shall collect any and all fees required by this article
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game
requires: collect any and all fees required by this article

provisions.what: All fees received by the department pursuant to this article shall be deposited in the account and shall be expended or encumbered to compensate persons who surrender permits pursuant to Section 7 or to provide for administration of this article
requires: shall be deposited in the account
shall be expended or encumbered to compensate persons who surrender permits pursuant to Section 7 or to provide for administration of this article

provisions.what: All funds received by the department during any fiscal year pursuant to this article which are not expended during that fiscal year shall be carried over into the following fiscal year and shall be used only for those purposes
requires: shall be carried over into the following fiscal year
forbids: use for other than those purposes

provisions.what: All interest accrued from the department’s retention of fees received pursuant to this article shall be credited to the account. The accrued interest may only be expended for the purposes authorized by this article
requires: shall be credited to the account
forbids: expending the accrued interest for purposes not authorized by this article

provisions.what: The account shall continue in existence, and the requirement to pay fees under this article shall remain in effect, until the compensation provided in Section 7 has been fully funded or until January 1, 1995, whichever occurs first

An amount, not to exceed 15 percent of the total annual revenues deposited in the account excluding any interest accrued or any funds carried over from a prior fiscal year may be expended for the administration of this article
conditions: not to exceed 15 percent of the total annual revenues deposited in the account excluding any interest accrued or any funds carried over from a prior fiscal year

provisions.what: A person taking fish from ocean waters south of a line extending due west from Point Arguello for sport purposes shall have permanently affixed to that person’s sportfishing license a marine resources protection stamp which may be obtained from the department upon payment of a fee of three dollars ($3)
provisions.binds: A person taking fish from ocean waters south of a line extending due west from Point Arguello for sport purposes
requires: In addition to a valid California sportfishing license and any applicable sport license stamp, a marine resources protection stamp permanently affixed to that person’s sportfishing license
conditions: upon payment of a fee of three dollars ($3)
exceptions: This subdivision does not apply to any one-day fishing license

provisions.what: The owner of any boat or vessel who, for profit, permits any person to fish from the boat or vessel in ocean waters south of a line extending due west from Point Arguello, shall obtain and permanently affix to the license a commercial marine resources protection stamp which may be obtained from the department upon payment of a fee of three dollars ($3)
provisions.binds: The owner of any boat or vessel who, for profit, permits any person to fish from the boat or vessel in ocean waters south of a line extending due west from Point Arguello
requires: In addition to a valid California commercial passenger fishing boat license, obtain and permanently affix to the license a commercial marine resources protection stamp
conditions: upon payment of a fee of three dollars ($3)

provisions.what: The department may accept contributions or donations from any person who wishes to donate money to be used for the compensation of commercial gill net and trammel net fishermen who surrender permits under this article
provisions.holder: The Department of Fish and Game

provisions.what: This section shall become inoperative on January 1, 1995

Any funds remaining in the Marine Resources Protection Account in the Fish and Game Preservation Fund on or after January 1, 1995, shall, with the approval of the Fish and Game Commission, be used to provide grants to colleges, universities and other bonafide scientific research groups to fund marine resource related scientific research within the ecological reserves established by Section 14 of this act
requires: be used to provide grants to colleges, universities and other bonafide scientific research groups to fund marine resource related scientific research within the ecological reserves established by Section 14 of this act
conditions: with the approval of the Fish and Game Commission

provisions.what: On or before December 31 of each year, the Director of Fish and Game shall prepare and submit a report to the Legislature regarding the implementation of this article including an accounting of all funds
provisions.binds: The Director of Fish and Game
requires: prepare and submit a report to the Legislature regarding the implementation of this article including an accounting of all funds

provisions.what: It is unlawful for any person to take, possess, receive, transport, purchase, sell, barter, or process any fish obtained in violation of this article
forbids: take, possess, receive, transport, purchase, sell, barter, or process any fish obtained in violation of this article

provisions.what: To increase the State’s scientific and biological information on the ocean fisheries of this State, the Department of Fish and Game shall establish a program whereby it can monitor and evaluate the daily landings of fish by commercial fishermen who are permitted under this article to take these fish
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game
requires: establish a program whereby it can monitor and evaluate the daily landings of fish by commercial fishermen who are permitted under this article to take these fish

provisions.what: The cost of implementing this monitoring program shall be borne by the commercial fishing industry
requires: The cost of implementing this monitoring program shall be borne by the commercial fishing industry

provisions.what: The penalty for a first violation of the provisions of Sections 3 and 4 of this article is a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) and not more than five thousand dollars ($5,000) and a mandatory suspension of any license, permit or stamp to take, receive, transport, purchase, sell, barter or process fish for commercial purposes for six months

The penalty for a second or subsequent violation of the provisions of Sections 3 and 4 of this article is a fine of not less than two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) and not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000) and a mandatory suspension of any license, permit or stamp to take, receive, transport, purchase, sell, barter, or process fish for commercial purposes for one year

Notwithstanding any other provisions of law, a violation of Section 8 of this article shall be deemed a violation of the provisions of Section 7145 of the Fish and Game Code and the penalty for such violation shall be consistent with the provisions of Section 12002.2 of said code

If a person convicted of a violation of Section 3, 4, or 8 of this article is granted probation, the court shall impose as a term or condition of probation, in addition to any other term or condition of probation, that the person pay at least the minimum fine prescribed in this section
requires: impose as a term or condition of probation that the person pay at least the minimum fine prescribed in this section
conditions: If a person convicted of a violation of Section 3, 4, or 8 of this article is granted probation

provisions.what: Prior to January 1, 1994, the Fish and Game Commission shall establish four new ecological reserves in ocean waters along the mainland coast
requires: establish four new ecological reserves in ocean waters along the mainland coast

provisions.what: Each ecological reserve shall have a surface area of at least two square miles
The commission shall restrict the use of these ecological reserves to scientific research relating to the management and enhancement of marine resources
requires: restrict the use of these ecological reserves to scientific research relating to the management and enhancement of marine resources

provisions.what: This article does not preempt or supersede any other closures to protect any other wildlife, including sea otters, whales, and shorebirds

If any provision of this article or the application thereof to any person or circumstances is held invalid, that invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this article which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this article are severable
conditions: If any provision of this article or the application thereof to any person or circumstances is held invalid

provisions.what: The State is divided into counties which are legal subdivisions of the State
The Legislature shall prescribe uniform procedure for county formation, consolidation, and boundary change
requires: prescribe uniform procedure for county formation, consolidation, and boundary change

provisions.what: Formation or consolidation requires approval by a majority of electors voting on the question in each affected county. A boundary change requires approval by the governing body of each affected county
requires: Formation or consolidation requires approval by a majority of electors voting on the question in each affected county
A boundary change requires approval by the governing body of each affected county

provisions.what: No county seat shall be removed unless two-thirds of the qualified electors of the county, voting on the proposition at a general election, shall vote in favor of such removal
forbids: removing a county seat
exceptions: unless two-thirds of the qualified electors of the county, voting on the proposition at a general election, shall vote in favor of such removal

provisions.what: A proposition of removal shall not be submitted in the same county more than once in four years
forbids: submitting a proposition of removal in the same county more than once in four years

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for county powers, an elected county sheriff, an elected district attorney, an elected assessor, and an elected governing body in each county
requires: provide for county powers, an elected county sheriff, an elected district attorney, an elected assessor, and an elected governing body in each county

provisions.what: Each governing body shall prescribe by ordinance the compensation of its members, but the ordinance prescribing such compensation shall be subject to referendum
requires: prescribe by ordinance the compensation of its members
the ordinance prescribing such compensation shall be subject to referendum
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (b) of Section 4 of this article

provisions.what: The Legislature or the governing body may provide for other officers whose compensation shall be prescribed by the governing body
provisions.holder: The Legislature or the governing body
requires: compensation shall be prescribed by the governing body

provisions.what: The governing body shall provide for the number, compensation, tenure, and appointment of employees
requires: provide for the number, compensation, tenure, and appointment of employees

provisions.what: The Legislature shall prescribe uniform procedure for city formation and provide for city powers
requires: prescribe uniform procedure for city formation
provide for city powers

provisions.what: A city may not be annexed to or consolidated into another
forbids: annexing a city to another
consolidating a city into another
exceptions: with approval by a majority of its electors voting on the question

provisions.what: For its own government, a county or city may adopt a charter by majority vote of its electors voting on the question
conditions: by majority vote of its electors voting on the question

provisions.what: The charter is effective when filed with the Secretary of State. A charter may be amended, revised, or repealed in the same manner
conditions: when filed with the Secretary of State

provisions.what: A charter, amendment, revision, or repeal thereof shall be published in the official state statutes
requires: shall be published in the official state statutes

provisions.what: County charters adopted pursuant to this section shall supersede any existing charter and all laws inconsistent therewith. The provisions of a charter are the law of the State and have the force and effect of legislative enactments
The governing body or charter commission of a county or city may propose a charter or revision
provisions.holder: The governing body or charter commission of a county or city

provisions.what: Amendment or repeal may be proposed by initiative or by the governing body
An election to determine whether to draft or revise a charter and elect a charter commission may be required by initiative or by the governing body
If provisions of 2 or more measures approved at the same election conflict, those of the measure receiving the highest affirmative vote shall prevail
conditions: If provisions of 2 or more measures approved at the same election conflict

provisions.what: County charters shall provide for a governing body of 5 or more members, elected (1) by district or, (2) at large, or (3) at large, with a requirement that they reside in a district
requires: A governing body of 5 or more members, elected (1) by district or, (2) at large, or (3) at large, with a requirement that they reside in a district

provisions.what: Charter counties are subject to statutes that relate to apportioning population of governing body districts
County charters shall provide for the compensation, terms, and removal of members of the governing body
requires: The compensation, terms, and removal of members of the governing body

provisions.what: If a county charter provides for the Legislature to prescribe the salary of the governing body, such compensation shall be prescribed by the governing body by ordinance
requires: such compensation shall be prescribed by the governing body by ordinance
conditions: If a county charter provides for the Legislature to prescribe the salary of the governing body

provisions.what: County charters shall provide for an elected sheriff, an elected district attorney, an elected assessor, other officers, their election or appointment, compensation, terms and removal
requires: An elected sheriff, an elected district attorney, an elected assessor, other officers, their election or appointment, compensation, terms and removal

provisions.what: County charters shall provide for the performance of functions required by statute
requires: The performance of functions required by statute

provisions.what: County charters shall provide for the powers and duties of governing bodies and all other county officers, and for consolidation and segregation of county officers, and for the manner of filling all vacancies occurring therein
requires: The powers and duties of governing bodies and all other county officers
consolidation and segregation of county officers
the manner of filling all vacancies occurring therein

provisions.what: County charters shall provide for the fixing and regulation by governing bodies, by ordinance, of the appointment and number of assistants, deputies, clerks, attachés, and other persons to be employed, and for the prescribing and regulating by such bodies of the powers, duties, qualifications, and compensation of such persons, the times at which, and terms for which they shall be appointed, and the manner of their appointment and removal
requires: The fixing and regulation by governing bodies, by ordinance, of the appointment and number of assistants, deputies, clerks, attachés, and other persons to be employed

the prescribing and regulating by such bodies of the powers, duties, qualifications, and compensation of such persons, the times at which, and terms for which they shall be appointed, and the manner of their appointment and removal

provisions.what: Whenever any county has framed and adopted a charter, and the same shall have been approved by the Legislature as herein provided, the general laws adopted by the Legislature in pursuance of Section 1(b) of this article, shall, as to such county, be superseded by said charter as to matters for which, under this section it is competent to make provision in such charter, and for which provision is made therein
conditions: Whenever any county has framed and adopted a charter, and the same shall have been approved by the Legislature as herein provided
exceptions: except as herein otherwise expressly provided

provisions.what: Charter counties shall have all the powers that are provided by this Constitution or by statute for counties

It shall be competent in any city charter to provide that the city governed thereunder may make and enforce all ordinances and regulations in respect to municipal affairs, subject only to restrictions and limitations provided in their several charters
conditions: subject only to restrictions and limitations provided in their several charters

provisions.what: In respect to other matters they shall be subject to general laws
requires: in respect to other matters they shall be subject to general laws

provisions.what: City charters adopted pursuant to this Constitution shall supersede any existing charter, and with respect to municipal affairs shall supersede all laws inconsistent therewith

It shall be competent in all city charters to provide, in addition to those provisions allowable by this Constitution, and by the laws of the State for: (1) the constitution, regulation, and government of the city police force (2) subgovernment in all or part of a city (3) conduct of city elections

Plenary authority is hereby granted, subject only to the restrictions of this article, to provide therein or by amendment thereto, the manner in which, the method by which, the times at which, and the terms for which the several municipal officers and employees whose compensation is paid by the city shall be elected or appointed, and for their removal, and for their compensation, and for the number of deputies, clerks and other employees that each shall have, and for the compensation, method of appointment, qualifications, tenure of office and removal of such deputies, clerks and other employees
conditions: subject only to the restrictions of this article

provisions.what: A county and all cities within it may consolidate as a charter city and county as provided by statute
provisions.holder: A county and all cities within it
conditions: as provided by statute

provisions.what: A charter city and county is a charter city and a charter county. Its charter city powers supersede conflicting charter county powers

No member may serve more than 2 terms

conditions: In the event a property tax is levied by the State

requires: This property shall be subject to taxation to the same extent and in the same manner as other property
exceptions: except franchises

forbids: Imposing on these companies any other tax or license charge which differs from that imposed on mercantile, manufacturing, and other business corporations

provisions.what: The Legislature may authorize Board assessment of property owned or used by other public utilities

The Legislature shall provide for an annual levy by county governing bodies of school district taxes sufficient to produce annual revenues for each district that the district’s board determines are required for its schools and district functions

conditions: If state boundaries change

forbids: Imposing taxes for local purposes

in the same fiscal year

requires: This full repayment shall be made not later than the end of the third fiscal year immediately following the fiscal year to which the modification applies
conditions: The Governor issues a proclamation that declares that, due to a severe state fiscal hardship, the suspension of subparagraph (A) is necessary

The Legislature enacts an urgency statute, pursuant to a bill passed in each house of the Legislature by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, that contains a suspension of subparagraph (A) for that fiscal year and does not contain any other provision

provisions.what: The Legislature shall not enact a statute to restrict the authority of a city, county, or city and county to impose a tax rate under, or change the method of distributing revenues derived under, the Bradley-Burns Uniform Local Sales and Use Tax Law, as that law read on November 3, 2004; the restriction also applies to the entitlement of a city, county, or city and county to the change in tax rate resulting from the end of the revenue exchange period
forbids: Restricting the authority of a city, county, or city and county to impose a tax rate under the Bradley-Burns Uniform Local Sales and Use Tax Law

provisions.what: The exchange under this subparagraph of revenues derived from a tax rate imposed under that law shall not require voter approval for the continued imposition of any portion of an existing tax rate from which those revenues are derived

exceptions: Except as otherwise provided in subparagraph (C) of paragraph (2)
pursuant to a bill passed in each house of the Legislature by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring

provisions.what: The Legislature shall not change the pro rata shares of ad valorem property tax pursuant to this paragraph, nor change the allocation of the revenues described in Section 15 of Article XI, to reimburse a local government when the Legislature or any state agency mandates a new program or higher level of service on that local government
forbids: Changing the pro rata shares of ad valorem property tax, or the allocation of the revenues described in Section 15 of Article XI, to reimburse a local government for a mandated new program or higher level of service

forbids: Reducing the payments to a city, county, or city and county that are required by Section 97.68 of the Revenue and Taxation Code

forbids: Restricting the authority of a local entity to impose a transactions and use tax rate
Changing the method for distributing revenues derived under a transaction and use tax rate

forbids: Requiring a community redevelopment agency to pay, remit, loan, or otherwise transfer such taxes to or for the benefit of the State, any agency of the State, or any jurisdiction
Requiring a community redevelopment agency to use, restrict, or assign a particular purpose for such taxes for the benefit of the State, any agency of the State, or any jurisdiction
exceptions: for making payments to affected taxing agencies pursuant to Sections 33607.5 and 33607.7 of the Health and Safety Code or similar statutes requiring such payments, as those statutes read on January 1, 2008
for the purpose of increasing, improving, and preserving the supply of low and moderate income housing available at affordable housing cost

provisions.what: For purposes of this section, the following definitions apply
terms: "Ad valorem property tax revenues": all revenues derived from the tax collected by a county under subdivision (a) of Section 1 of Article XIII A, regardless of any of this revenue being otherwise classified by statute
"Local agency": has the same meaning as specified in Section 95 of the Revenue and Taxation Code as that section read on November 3, 2004
"Jurisdiction": has the same meaning as specified in Section 95 of the Revenue and Taxation Code as that section read on November 3, 2004

provisions.what: Taxes on or measured by income may be imposed on persons, corporations, or other entities as prescribed by law
conditions: as prescribed by law

provisions.what: Interest on bonds issued by the State or a local government in the State is exempt from taxes on income
Income of a nonprofit educational institution of collegiate grade within the State of California is exempt from taxes on or measured by income if both of the following conditions are met
conditions: The income is not unrelated business income as defined by the Legislature
The income is used exclusively for educational purposes

provisions.what: A nonprofit organization that is exempted from taxation by Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 23701) of Part 11 of Division 2 of the Revenue and Taxation Code or Subchapter F (commencing with Section 501) of Chapter 1 of Subtitle A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or the successor of either, is exempt from any business license tax or fee measured by income or gross receipts that is levied by a county or city, whether charter or general law, a city and county, a school district, a special district, or any other local agency

conditions: a majority of the membership of each house concurring
by any method not prohibited by this Constitution or the Constitution or laws of the United States

provisions.what: The tax on state and national banks shall be according to or measured by their net income and shall be in lieu of all other taxes and license fees upon banks or their shares
conditions: Unless otherwise provided by the Legislature
exceptions: except taxes upon real property and vehicle registration and license fees

terms: "Insurer": includes insurance companies or associations and reciprocal or interinsurance exchanges together with their corporate or other attorneys in fact considered as a single unit, and the State Compensation Insurance Fund
"companies": includes persons, partnerships, joint stock associations, companies and corporations

The basis of the annual tax for an insurer not transacting title insurance is the amount of gross premiums, less return premiums, received in such year upon its business done in this State, other than premiums received for reinsurance and for ocean marine insurance; for an insurer transacting title insurance it is all income upon business done in this State, with exceptions
exceptions: Interest and dividends
Rents from real property
Profits from the sale or other disposition of investments
Income from investments

there shall be excluded from the basis of the annual tax imposed by this section, the income of, and from the assets of, such trust department and such trust business, if such income is taxed by this State or included in the measure of any tax imposed by this State
terms: "basis of the annual tax": for an insurer not transacting title insurance, the amount of gross premiums, less return premiums, received in such year by such insurer upon its business done in this State, other than premiums received for reinsurance and for ocean marine insurance; for an insurer transacting title insurance, all income upon business done in this State, except as listed
"Investments": includes property acquired by such insurer in the settlement or adjustment of claims against it but excludes investments in title plants and title records

provisions.what: The rate of the tax to be applied to the basis of the annual tax in respect to each year is 2.35 percent
The tax imposed on insurers by this section is in lieu of all other taxes and licenses, state, county, and municipal, upon such insurers and their property
exceptions: Taxes upon their real estate

That an insurer transacting title insurance in this State which has a trust department or does a trust business under the banking laws of this State is subject to taxation with respect to such trust department or trust business to the same extent and in the same manner as trust companies and the trust departments of banks doing business in this State
The retaliatory taxes, licenses, fees, fines, penalties, deposit requirements or other obligations described in paragraph (3)
The tax on ocean marine insurance
Motor vehicle and other vehicle registration license fees and any other tax or license fee imposed by the State upon vehicles, motor vehicles or the operation thereof

That each corporate or other attorney in fact of a reciprocal or interinsurance exchange shall be subject to all taxes imposed upon corporations or others doing business in the State, other than taxes on income derived from its principal business as attorney in fact

provisions.what: When by or pursuant to the laws of any other state or foreign country any taxes, licenses and other fees, fines, penalties, deposit requirements or other material obligations, prohibitions or restrictions are or would be imposed upon California insurers in excess of those directly imposed upon similar insurers of such other state or country under the statutes of this State, the same taxes, licenses and other fees, fines, penalties or deposit requirements or other material obligations, prohibitions, or restrictions shall be imposed upon the insurers of such other state or country doing business or seeking to do business in California
requires: deductions, from premium taxes or other taxes otherwise payable, allowed on account of real estate or personal property taxes paid shall be taken into consideration in determining the propriety and extent of retaliatory action under this paragraph (3) of subdivision (f)

conditions: so long as such laws of such other state or country continue in force or are so applied
exceptions: The provisions of this paragraph (3) of subdivision (f) shall not apply as to personal income taxes, nor as to ad valorem taxes on real or personal property nor as to special purpose obligations or assessments heretofore imposed by another state or foreign country in connection with particular kinds of insurance, other than property insurance

"domicile": of an alien insurer, other than insurers formed under the laws of Canada, the state in which is located its principal place of business in the United States; of an insurer formed under the laws of Canada or a province thereof, the province in which its head office is situated

provisions.binds: A corporate or other attorney in fact of each exchange

provisions.what: Every insurer transacting the business of ocean marine insurance in this State shall annually pay to the State a tax measured by that proportion of the underwriting profit of such insurer from such insurance written in the United States, which the gross premiums of the insurer from such insurance written in this State bear to the gross premiums of the insurer from such insurance written within the United States, at the rate of 5 per centum, which tax shall be in lieu of all other taxes and licenses, state, county and municipal, upon such insurer
provisions.binds: Every insurer transacting the business of ocean marine insurance in this State
exceptions: except taxes upon real estate, and such other taxes as may be assessed or levied against such insurer on account of any other class of insurance written by it

provisions.what: The Legislature shall define the terms "ocean marine insurance" and "underwriting profit," and shall provide for the assessment, levy, collection and enforcement of the ocean marine tax
The taxes provided for by this section shall be assessed by the State Board of Equalization

conditions: a majority of all the members elected to each of the two houses voting in favor thereof

provisions.what: This section is not intended to and does not change the law as it has previously existed with respect to the meaning of the words "gross premiums, less return premiums, received" as used in this article

requires: Before the contract becomes operative, it shall be authorized by a majority of those voting on the question in each jurisdiction at a general or direct primary election

provisions.holder: Counties, cities and counties, and cities
conditions: if the ordinance or resolution proposing each contract is approved by a two-thirds vote of the governing body of each jurisdiction that is a party to the contract

provisions.what: The power to tax may not be surrendered or suspended by grant or contract
forbids: Surrendering or suspending the power to tax by grant or contract

forbids: Legal or equitable process against this State or any officer thereof to prevent or enjoin the collection of any tax

conditions: After payment of a tax claimed to be illegal
in such manner as may be provided by the Legislature

provisions.what: The Legislature shall pass all laws necessary to carry out the provisions of this article

provisions.binds: The State of California and its political subdivisions
forbids: Levying or collecting a sales or use tax on the sale of, or the storage, use or other consumption in this State of food products for human consumption
exceptions: except as provided by statute as of the effective date of this section

provisions.what: The people of the State of California find and declare that public safety services are critically important; that the protection of the public safety is the first responsibility of local government and local officials have an obligation to give priority to the provision of adequate public safety services; and that the proceeds of the tax enacted pursuant to this section shall be designated exclusively for public safety

In addition to any sales and use taxes imposed by the Legislature, a tax is hereby imposed upon all retailers at the rate of 1/2 percent of the gross receipts from the sale of all tangible personal property sold at retail in this State on and after January 1, 1994, and an excise tax is hereby imposed on the storage, use, or other consumption in this State of tangible personal property purchased from any retailer on and after January 1, 1994, at the rate of 1/2 percent of the sales price of the property
The Sales and Use Tax Law, including any amendments made thereto on or after the effective date of this section, shall be applicable to the taxes imposed by subdivision (b)

All revenues, less refunds, derived from the taxes imposed pursuant to subdivision (b) shall be transferred to the Local Public Safety Fund for allocation by the Legislature, as prescribed by statute, to counties in which either of the following occurs
conditions: The board of supervisors, by a majority vote of its membership, requests an allocation from the Local Public Safety Fund in a manner prescribed by statute
A majority of the county’s voters voting thereon approve the addition of this section

provisions.what: Moneys in the Local Public Safety Fund shall be allocated for use exclusively for public safety services of local agencies
requires: use exclusively for public safety services of local agencies

provisions.what: Revenues derived from the taxes imposed pursuant to subdivision (b) shall not be considered proceeds of taxes for purposes of Article XIII B or State General Fund proceeds of taxes within the meaning of Article XVI
This section shall supersede any other provisions of this Constitution that are in conflict with the provisions of this section, including, but not limited to, Section 9 of Article II
exceptions: Except for the provisions of Section 34

provisions.what: For purposes of this section, "Public Safety Services" includes the listed services
terms: "Public Safety Services": includes employing and training public safety officials; managing local jails and providing housing, treatment, and services for, and supervision of, juvenile and adult offenders; preventing child abuse, neglect, or exploitation and providing related services, adoption services, and adult protective services; providing mental health services to children and adults; and preventing, treating, and providing recovery services for substance abuse

provisions.what: "2011 Realignment Legislation" means legislation enacted on or before September 30, 2012, to implement the state budget plan, that is entitled 2011 Realignment and provides for the assignment of Public Safety Services responsibilities to local agencies
terms: "2011 Realignment Legislation": legislation enacted on or before September 30, 2012, to implement the state budget plan, that is entitled 2011 Realignment and provides for the assignment of Public Safety Services responsibilities to local agencies, including related reporting responsibilities

provisions.what: The legislation shall provide local agencies with maximum flexibility and control over the design, administration, and delivery of Public Safety Services consistent with federal law and funding requirements, as determined by the Legislature
2011 Realignment Legislation shall include no new programs assigned to local agencies after January 1, 2012
exceptions: except for the early periodic screening, diagnosis, and treatment (EPSDT) program and mental health managed care

provisions.what: Commencing in the 2011–12 fiscal year and continuing thereafter, all revenues, less refunds, derived from the taxes described in Sections 6051.15 and 6201.15 of the Revenue and Taxation Code and from the vehicle license fees described in Section 11005 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, as those sections read on July 1, 2011, shall be deposited into the Local Revenue Fund 2011
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (d)

provisions.what: On and after July 1, 2011, the revenues deposited pursuant to paragraph (1) shall not be considered General Fund revenues or proceeds of taxes for purposes of Section 8 of Article XVI of the California Constitution

Funds deposited in the Local Revenue Fund 2011 are continuously appropriated exclusively to fund the provision of Public Safety Services by local agencies; pending full implementation of the 2011 Realignment Legislation, funds may also be used to reimburse the State for program costs incurred in providing Public Safety Services on behalf of local agencies
requires: The methodology for allocating funds shall be as specified in the 2011 Realignment Legislation

provisions.what: The county treasurer, city and county treasurer, or other appropriate official shall create a County Local Revenue Fund 2011 within the treasury of each county or city and county
provisions.binds: The county treasurer, city and county treasurer, or other appropriate official
requires: The money in each County Local Revenue Fund 2011 shall be exclusively used to fund the provision of Public Safety Services by local agencies as specified by the 2011 Realignment Legislation

provisions.what: A mandate of a new program or higher level of service on a local agency imposed by the 2011 Realignment Legislation, or by any regulation, executive order or administrative directive issued to implement that legislation, shall not constitute a mandate requiring the State to provide a subvention of funds; any requirement that a local agency comply with Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 54950) of Part 1 of Division 2 of Title 5 of the Government Code shall not be a reimbursable mandate under Section 6 of Article XIII B

provisions.what: Legislation enacted after September 30, 2012, that has an overall effect of increasing the costs already borne by a local agency for programs or levels of service mandated by the 2011 Realignment Legislation shall apply to local agencies only to the extent that the State provides annual funding for the cost increase; local agencies shall not be obligated to provide programs or levels of service required by such legislation above the level for which funding has been provided

exceptions: This paragraph shall not apply to legislation currently exempt from subvention under paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) of Section 6 of Article XIII B as that paragraph read on January 2, 2011

provisions.what: The State shall not submit to the federal government any plans or waivers, or amendments to those plans or waivers, that have an overall effect of increasing the cost borne by a local agency for programs or levels of service mandated by the 2011 Realignment Legislation

provisions.what: The State shall not be required to provide a subvention of funds pursuant to this paragraph for a mandate that is imposed by the State at the request of a local agency or to comply with federal law

conditions: For programs described in subparagraphs (C) to (E), inclusive, of paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) and included in the 2011 Realignment Legislation

provisions.what: When the State is a party to any complaint brought in a federal judicial or administrative proceeding that involves one or more of those programs, and there is a settlement or judicial or administrative order that imposes a cost in the form of a monetary penalty or has the overall effect of increasing the costs already borne by a local agency for programs or levels of service mandated by the 2011 Realignment Legislation, the State shall annually provide at least 50 percent of the nonfederal share of those costs as determined by the State
requires: The state funds provided in this paragraph shall be from funding sources other than those described in subdivisions (b) and (d), ad valorem property taxes, or the Social Services Subaccount of the Sales Tax Account of the Local Revenue Fund

provisions.what: If the State or a local agency fails to perform a duty or obligation under this section or under the 2011 Realignment Legislation, an appropriate party may seek judicial relief
requires: These proceedings shall have priority over all other civil matters
conditions: If the State or a local agency fails to perform a duty or obligation under this section or under the 2011 Realignment Legislation

provisions.what: The funds deposited into a County Local Revenue Fund 2011 shall be spent in a manner designed to maintain the State’s eligibility for federal matching funds, and to ensure compliance by the State with applicable federal standards governing the State’s provision of Public Safety Services
The funds deposited into a County Local Revenue Fund 2011 shall not be used by local agencies to supplant other funding for Public Safety Services
forbids: Using the funds to supplant other funding for Public Safety Services

provisions.what: If the taxes described in subdivision (b) are reduced or cease to be operative, the State shall annually provide moneys to the Local Revenue Fund 2011 in an amount equal to or greater than the aggregate amount that otherwise would have been provided by the taxes described in subdivision (b)
requires: The method for determining that amount shall be described in the 2011 Realignment Legislation
the State shall be obligated to provide that amount for so long as the local agencies are required to perform the Public Safety Services responsibilities assigned by the 2011 Realignment Legislation
conditions: If the taxes described in subdivision (b) are reduced or cease to be operative

conditions: If the State fails to annually appropriate that amount

provisions.what: The state obligations under this subdivision shall have a lower priority claim to General Fund money than the first priority for money to be set apart under Section 8 of Article XVI and the second priority to pay voter-approved debts and liabilities described in Section 1 of Article XVI

The Education Protection Account is hereby created in the General Fund to receive and disburse the revenues derived from the incremental increases in taxes imposed by this section, as specified in subdivision (f)

Before June 30, 2013, and before June 30 of each year from 2014 to 2030, inclusive, the Director of Finance shall estimate the total amount of additional revenues, less refunds, that will be derived from the incremental increases in tax rates made in subdivision (f) that will be available for transfer into the Education Protection Account during the next fiscal year; and shall make the same estimate by January 10, 2013, for revenues to be received by the end of the 2012–13 fiscal year

During the last 10 days of the quarter of each of the first three quarters of each fiscal year from 2013–14 to 2030–31, inclusive, the Controller shall transfer into the Education Protection Account one-fourth of the total amount estimated pursuant to subparagraph (A) for that fiscal year
exceptions: except as this amount may be adjusted pursuant to subparagraph (D)

provisions.what: In each of the fiscal years from 2012–13 to 2032–33, inclusive, the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjustment to the Education Protection Account by adding together the recalculated estimate, less amounts previously transferred, and the final determination of revenues for the fiscal year ending two years prior, less the updated estimate for that year
requires: In the last quarter of each fiscal year from 2012–13 to 2030–31, inclusive, the Director of Finance shall recalculate the estimate made for the fiscal year pursuant to subparagraph (A), and shall subtract from this updated estimate the amounts previously transferred to the Education Protection Account for that fiscal year

In June 2015 and in every June from 2016 to 2033, inclusive, the Director of Finance shall make a final determination of the amount of additional revenues, less refunds, derived from the incremental increases in tax rates made in subdivision (f) for the fiscal year ending two years prior

provisions.what: If the sum determined pursuant to subparagraph (C) is positive, the Controller shall transfer an amount equal to that sum into the Education Protection Account within 10 days preceding the end of the fiscal year; if that amount is negative, the Controller shall suspend or reduce subsequent quarterly transfers, if any, until the total reduction equals the negative amount
requires: For purposes of any calculation made pursuant to clause (i) of subparagraph (C), the amount of a quarterly transfer shall not be modified to reflect any suspension or reduction made pursuant to this subparagraph

provisions.what: Before June 30, 2018, and before June 30 of each year from 2019 to 2030, inclusive, the Director of Finance shall estimate the amount of the additional revenues, less refunds, to be derived in the following fiscal year from the incremental increases in tax rates made in subdivision (f), that, when combined with all other available General Fund revenues, will be required to meet the minimum funding guarantee of Section 8 of Article XVI and the workload budget for that following fiscal year
terms: "workload budget": has the meaning set forth in Section 13308.05 of the Government Code, as that section read and was interpreted by the Department of Finance on January 1, 2016
"currently authorized services": only those services that would have been considered "currently authorized services" under Section 13308.05 of the Government Code as of January 1, 2016

provisions.what: Whenever the Director of Finance estimates that the amount available for transfer into the Education Protection Account during the following fiscal year exceeds the amount of revenues required from that account pursuant to subparagraph (E), the director shall identify the remaining amount; fifty percent of that remainder, up to a maximum of two billion dollars in any single fiscal year, shall be allocated by the Controller from the Education Protection Account to the California Department of Health Care Services on a quarterly basis to increase funding for the existing health care programs and services described
provisions.binds: The Director of Finance and the Controller
requires: The funding shall be used only for critical, emergency, acute, and preventive health care services to children and their families, provided by health care professionals and health facilities that are licensed pursuant to Section 1250 of the Health and Safety Code, and to health plans or others that manage the provision of health care for Medi-Cal beneficiaries that are contracting with the California Department of Health Care Services to provide health benefits pursuant to this section

provisions.what: The allocation provided for in subparagraph (F) may be suspended by statute during a fiscal year in which a budget emergency has been declared
requires: the allocation shall not be reduced beyond the proportional reduction in overall General Fund expenditures for that year
terms: "budget emergency": has the same meaning as in paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 22 of Article XVI

provisions.what: The funding provided pursuant to subparagraph (F) shall not be used to supplant existing state General Funds for the nonfederal share of payments for those programs and, consistent with federal law, shall be used to obtain federal matching Medicaid funds
requires: consistent with federal law, shall be used to obtain federal matching Medicaid funds
forbids: Using the funding to supplant existing state General Funds for the nonfederal share of payments for those programs

provisions.what: All moneys in the Education Protection Account are hereby continuously appropriated for the support of school districts, county offices of education, charter schools, and community college districts as set forth in this paragraph, and for health care as set forth in subparagraph (F) of paragraph (2)

Eleven percent of the moneys appropriated for education pursuant to this paragraph shall be allocated quarterly by the Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges to community college districts to provide general purpose funding in proportion to the amounts determined pursuant to Section 84750.5 of the Education Code, as that code section read on November 6, 2012
provisions.binds: The Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges
requires: The allocations shall be offset by the amounts specified in subdivisions (a), (c), and (d) of Section 84751 of the Education Code that are in excess of the amounts calculated pursuant to Section 84750.5
no community college district shall receive less than one hundred dollars ($100) per full time equivalent student

provisions.what: Eighty-nine percent of the moneys appropriated for education pursuant to this paragraph shall be allocated quarterly by the Superintendent of Public Instruction to provide general purpose funding to school districts, county offices of education, and state general-purpose funding to charter schools in proportion to the revenue limits and amounts calculated pursuant to Sections 2558, 42238 and 47633 of the Education Code, as those sections read on November 6, 2012
requires: The amounts so calculated shall be offset by the amounts specified in the listed sections of the Education Code that are in excess of the amounts calculated pursuant to Sections 2558, 42238, and 47633
no school district, county office of education, or charter school shall receive less than two hundred dollars ($200) per unit of average daily attendance

provisions.what: This subdivision is self-executing and requires no legislative action to take effect. Distribution of the moneys in the Education Protection Account by the Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges and Superintendent of Public Instruction shall not be delayed or otherwise affected by failure of the Legislature and Governor to enact an annual budget bill pursuant to Section 12 of Article IV, by invocation of subdivision (h) of Section 8 of Article XVI, or by any other action or failure to act by the Legislature or Governor
The moneys deposited in the Education Protection Account for education shall not be used to pay any costs incurred by the Legislature, the Governor, or any agency of state government
forbids: Using the moneys to pay any costs incurred by the Legislature, the Governor, or any agency of state government
exceptions: Notwithstanding any other provision of law

provisions.what: A community college district, county office of education, school district, or charter school shall have sole authority to determine how the moneys received from the Education Protection Account are spent in the school or schools within its jurisdiction
provisions.holder: A community college district, county office of education, school district, or charter school
forbids: Using any of the funds from the Education Protection Account for salaries or benefits of administrators or any other administrative costs
conditions: the appropriate governing board or body shall make these spending determinations in open session of a public meeting of the governing board or body

provisions.what: Each community college district, county office of education, school district, and charter school shall annually publish on its Internet Web site an accounting of how much money was received from the Education Protection Account and how that money was spent
provisions.binds: Each community college district, county office of education, school district, and charter school

provisions.what: The annual independent financial and compliance audit required of community college districts, county offices of education, school districts, and charter schools shall, in addition to all other requirements of law, ascertain and verify whether the funds provided from the Education Protection Account have been properly disbursed and expended as required by this section
requires: Expenses incurred by those entities to comply with the additional audit requirement of this section may be paid with funding from the Education Protection Account and shall not be considered administrative costs for purposes of this section

provisions.what: Revenues, less refunds, derived pursuant to subdivision (f) for deposit in the Education Protection Account shall be deemed "General Fund revenues," "General Fund proceeds of taxes," and "moneys to be applied by the State for the support of school districts and community college districts" for purposes of Section 8 of Article XVI

In addition to the taxes imposed by Part 1 (commencing with Section 6001) of Division 2 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, a tax is hereby imposed upon all retailers at the rate of 1/4 percent of the gross receipts from the sale of all tangible personal property sold at retail in this State on and after January 1, 2013, and before January 1, 2017, and an excise tax is hereby imposed on the storage, use, or other consumption in this State of such property at the rate of 1/4 percent of the sales price of the property
requires: The Sales and Use Tax Law, including any amendments enacted on or after the effective date of this section, shall apply to the taxes imposed pursuant to this paragraph
conditions: This paragraph shall become inoperative on January 1, 2017

provisions.what: For any taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 2012, and before January 1, 2031, the income tax bracket and the rate of 9.3 percent set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) of Section 17041 of the Revenue and Taxation Code shall be modified so that the tax rate is 10.3 percent of taxable income over $250,000 but not over $300,000, 11.3 percent over $300,000 but not over $500,000, and 12.3 percent over $500,000, of the excess over each amount
requires: The income tax brackets shall be recomputed, as otherwise provided in subdivision (h) of Section 17041 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, only for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2013
For purposes of subdivision (g) of Section 19136 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, this paragraph shall be considered to be chaptered on November 6, 2012
the modified tax brackets and tax rates established and imposed by this paragraph shall be deemed to be established and imposed under Section 17041 of the Revenue and Taxation Code
conditions: This paragraph shall become inoperative on December 1, 2031

provisions.what: For any taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 2012, and before January 1, 2031, the income tax bracket and the rate of 9.3 percent set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of Section 17041 of the Revenue and Taxation Code shall be modified so that the tax rate is 10.3 percent of taxable income over $340,000 but not over $408,000, 11.3 percent over $408,000 but not over $680,000, and 12.3 percent over $680,000, of the excess over each amount
requires: The income tax brackets shall be recomputed, as otherwise provided in subdivision (h) of Section 17041 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, only for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2013
For purposes of subdivision (g) of Section 19136 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, this paragraph shall be considered to be chaptered on November 6, 2012
the modified tax brackets and tax rates established and imposed by this paragraph shall be deemed to be established and imposed under Section 17041 of the Revenue and Taxation Code
conditions: This paragraph shall become inoperative on December 1, 2031

provisions.what: The Controller, pursuant to his or her statutory authority, may perform audits of expenditures from the Local Revenue Fund 2011 and any County Local Revenue Fund 2011
The Controller shall audit the Education Protection Account to ensure that those funds are used and accounted for in a manner consistent with this section
The Attorney General or local district attorney shall expeditiously investigate any misuse of moneys from the County Local Revenue Fund 2011 or the Education Protection Account
provisions.binds: The Attorney General or local district attorney

provisions.what: The Attorney General or local district attorney may seek civil or criminal penalties for any misuse of moneys from the County Local Revenue Fund 2011 or the Education Protection Account
provisions.holder: The Attorney General or local district attorney

provisions.what: The maximum amount of any ad valorem tax on real property shall not exceed One percent (1%) of the full cash value of such property
forbids: Any ad valorem tax on real property exceeding One percent (1%) of the full cash value of such property

provisions.what: The one percent (1%) tax to be collected by the counties and apportioned according to law to the districts within the counties
The limitation provided for in subdivision (a) shall not apply to ad valorem taxes or special assessments to pay the interest and redemption charges on any of the following
exceptions: Indebtedness approved by the voters prior to July 1, 1978
Bonded indebtedness for the acquisition or improvement of real property approved on or after July 1, 1978, by two-thirds of the votes cast by the voters voting on the proposition

Bonded indebtedness incurred by a school district, community college district, or county office of education for the construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, or replacement of school facilities, including the furnishing and equipping of school facilities, or the acquisition or lease of real property for school facilities, approved by 55 percent of the voters of the district or county, as appropriate, voting on the proposition on or after the effective date of the measure adding this paragraph

provisions.what: This paragraph shall apply only if the proposition approved by the voters and resulting in the bonded indebtedness includes all of the following accountability requirements
requires: A requirement that the proceeds from the sale of the bonds be used only for the purposes specified in Article XIII A, Section 1(b)(3), and not for any other purpose, including teacher and administrator salaries and other school operating expenses

A list of the specific school facilities projects to be funded and certification that the school district board, community college board, or county office of education has evaluated safety, class size reduction, and information technology needs in developing that list

A requirement that the school district board, community college board, or county office of education conduct an annual, independent performance audit to ensure that the funds have been expended only on the specific projects listed

A requirement that the school district board, community college board, or county office of education conduct an annual, independent financial audit of the proceeds from the sale of the bonds until all of those proceeds have been expended for the school facilities projects

provisions.what: Notwithstanding any other provisions of law or of this Constitution, school districts, community college districts, and county offices of education may levy a 55 percent vote ad valorem tax pursuant to subdivision (b)
provisions.holder: School districts, community college districts, and county offices of education

provisions.what: The full cash value means the county assessor’s valuation of real property as shown on the 1975–76 tax bill under full cash value or, thereafter, the appraised value of real property when purchased, newly constructed, or a change in ownership has occurred after the 1975 assessment. All real property not already assessed up to the 1975–76 full cash value may be reassessed to reflect that valuation
terms: "full cash value": the county assessor’s valuation of real property as shown on the 1975–76 tax bill under "full cash value" or, thereafter, the appraised value of real property when purchased, newly constructed, or a change in ownership has occurred after the 1975 assessment

"newly constructed": does not include real property that is reconstructed after a disaster, as declared by the Governor, where the fair market value of the real property, as reconstructed, is comparable to its fair market value prior to the disaster; and does not include that portion of an existing structure that consists of the construction or reconstruction of seismic retrofitting components, as defined by the Legislature

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide that, under appropriate circumstances and pursuant to definitions and procedures established by the Legislature, any person over the age of 55 years who resides in property that is eligible for the homeowner’s exemption may transfer the base year value of the property entitled to exemption, with the adjustments authorized by subdivision (b), to any replacement dwelling of equal or lesser value located within the same county and purchased or newly constructed by that person as his or her principal residence within two years of the sale of the original property
conditions: This paragraph shall apply to any replacement dwelling that was purchased or newly constructed on or after November 5, 1986
terms: "any person over the age of 55 years": includes a married couple one member of which is over the age of 55 years
"replacement dwelling": a building, structure, or other shelter constituting a place of abode, whether real property or personal property, and any land on which it may be situated
"two-dwelling unit": shall be considered as two separate single-family dwellings

provisions.what: The Legislature may authorize each county board of supervisors, after consultation with the local affected agencies within the county’s boundaries, to adopt an ordinance making the provisions of this subdivision relating to transfer of base year value also applicable to situations in which the replacement dwellings are located in that county and the original properties are located in another county within this State
conditions: This paragraph applies to any replacement dwelling that was purchased or newly constructed on or after the date the county adopted the provisions of this subdivision relating to transfer of base year value, but does not apply to any replacement dwelling that was purchased or newly constructed before November 9, 1988
terms: "local affected agency": any city, special district, school district, or community college district that receives an annual property tax revenue allocation

provisions.what: The Legislature may extend the provisions of this subdivision relating to the transfer of base year values from original properties to replacement dwellings of homeowners over the age of 55 years to severely disabled homeowners
conditions: but only with respect to those replacement dwellings purchased or newly constructed on or after the effective date of this paragraph

provisions.what: The full cash value base may reflect from year to year the inflationary rate not to exceed 2 percent for any given year or reduction as shown in the consumer price index or comparable data for the area under taxing jurisdiction, or may be reduced to reflect substantial damage, destruction, or other factors causing a decline in value

For purposes of subdivision (a), the Legislature may provide that the term newly constructed does not include any of the following: the construction or addition of any active solar energy system; certain fire sprinkler, fire extinguishing, fire detection systems or fire-related egress improvements; certain construction to make a dwelling more accessible to a severely disabled person; certain construction to make a building more accessible to, or more usable by, a disabled person; and the construction or addition, completed on or after January 1, 2019, of a rain water capture system

For purposes of this section, the term change in ownership does not include the acquisition of real property as a replacement for comparable property if the person acquiring the real property has been displaced from the property replaced by eminent domain proceedings, by acquisition by a public entity, or governmental action that has resulted in a judgment of inverse condemnation
conditions: This subdivision applies to any property acquired after March 1, 1975, but affects only those assessments of that property that occur after the provisions of this subdivision take effect
terms: "comparable": the real property acquired shall be deemed comparable to the property replaced if it is similar in size, utility, and function, or if it conforms to state regulations defined by the Legislature governing the relocation of persons displaced by governmental actions

provisions.what: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, the Legislature shall provide that the base year value of property that is substantially damaged or destroyed by a disaster, as declared by the Governor, may be transferred to comparable property within the same county that is acquired or newly constructed as a replacement for the substantially damaged or destroyed property
conditions: Except as provided in paragraph (3), this subdivision applies to any comparable replacement property acquired or newly constructed on or after July 1, 1985, and to the determination of base year values for the 1985–86 fiscal year and fiscal years thereafter
